title.narrative: Peace Building and Community Cohesion Project, Fas 2
Peace Building and Community Cohesion Project, Phase 2

description.narrative:
Sida har stött UNDP och dess arbete för fred och sammanhållning på lokalsamhällesnivå i Sudsudan sedan 2014, i projektet Commuity Security and Arms Control 2014-2016 (40 MSEK) följt av fas 1 av Peace and Community Cohesion, 2017-2020 (60 MSEK). Ett projektförslag för PaCC fas 2 inkom till Sida 12 februari 2020. Förutom projektdokumentet har beredningen av insatsen grundats på den externa utvärderingen av fas 1 och de årliga resultatrapporterna från fas 1.
PaCC II bygger på de tidigare två projekten. De tre projekten formar sammantaget en långsiktig strävan av UNDP att skapa en gynnsam miljö för genomförandet av det nu gällande fredsavtalet mellan regering och väpnad opposition - the Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan, R-ARCSS - och tidigare fredsavtal. Det nya projektet kommer att både fördjupa och utvidga redan pågående initiativ för att bygga fred och sammanhållning från gräsrotsnivå och uppåt till central nivå i samhället. Pågående verksamhet under PaCC I kommer att fördjupas i de fem geografiska konfliktområden (conflict clusters) där UNDP redan arbetar och också utvidgas till två ytterligare konfliktområden.
Projektets övergripande mål (outcome) är att, i enlighet med UNDP:s landprogram för Sydsudan, Sydsudans befolkning och då i synnerhet de mest sårbara grupperna kan dra nytta av vad UNDP benämner en stärkt infrastruktur för fred, ökad sammanhållning, försoning och tillit samt stärkt ansvarsutkrävande på alla nivåer. Målet kommer att nås via tre resultat: 1. Infrastrukturen för fred (institutioner, lagstiftining, personal etc) på lokal och central nivå är formade så att de har förmågan att hantera konflikter och främja fredlig samexistens; 2. Lokalsamhällena har fungerande strukturer som uppmuntrar och främjar traumabearbetning, försoning och våldsreducering och som stärker social sammanhållning; 3. Fredsprocesser har ett integrerat jämställdhetsperspektiv och förutsättningarna för kvinnors, ungas och minoriteters deltagande i beslutsfattande har stärkts.
De huvudsakliga målgrupperna för insatsen är unga, kvinnor och flickor, människor med funktionsnedsättning samt minoritetsgrupper i sju olika geografiska konfliktområden kring Bor, Wau, Aweil, Bentiu, Malakal, Torit och Rumbek. Beteenden och värderingar i lokalsamhällena kommer att ändras genom stärkande av dessa gruppers deltgande i beslutsfattande och andra viktiga samhällsprocesser .
PaCC II är ett brett, omfattande projekt som syftar till att stärka sambanden mellan det humanitära biståndet, utvecklings- och fredsarbetet, dvs det som benämns trippel-nexus. Projektet innehåller stöd till såväl konfliktförebyggande, medling och annat fredsskapande som tidig återuppbyggnad, i syfte att minska risken för våldsam konflikt och kriser, vilka skapar behov av humanitär hjälp och undergräver utveckling.
Det fyraåriga projektets totala budget är 35 MUSD, motsvarande cirka 315 MSEK. Det föreslagna bidraget från Sida är 120 MSEK över de fyra åren, från juni 2020 till mars 2024. Det utgör cirka 33% av den totala budgeten. Andra biståndsgivare är Japan, KOICA (Sydkorea) och Afrikanska utvecklingsbanken.

Sida has been supporting UNDP and its work for peace and community cohesion in South Sudan since 2014, in the Community Security and Arms Control project 2014-2016 (40 MSEK) followed by the Peace and Community Cohesion project (PaCC) 2017-2020 (60 MSEK). A proposal for PaCC Phase II was submitted to Sida on 12 February 2020. In addition to the Project Document, the appraisal was based on an external evaluation of PaCC Phase I, dated January 2020, and narrative and financial reports of Phase I.
PaCC II is built on the previous two projects. The three projects taken together form a long term effort of UNDP to promoting a conducive environment for successful implementation of the Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan, R-ARCSS, and previous peace agreements. The new project will deepen and expand on ongoing initiatives to build peace and cohesion from the grassroots to the national level. Ongoing activities under PaCC I will be deepened in the currently targeted conflict clusters (geographical areas), and be expanded to at least two more conflict clusters.
The overarching objective (outcome) of the project, aligned with the UNDP South Sudan Country Programme Document, is that the South Sudanese population, particularly the most vulnerable groups, benefit from strengthened peace infrastructures, increased cohesion, reconciliation, trust and accountable governance at all levels. This goal will be reached through achievement of three outputs:
1. Infrastructures of peace at the central and local levels are enabled to manage conflicts and foster peaceful co-existence;
2. Communities have structures to encourage trauma healing, reconciliation, violence reduction and reinforce social cohesion;
3. Peace processes are engendered and conditions of women, youth and minority participation in decision making improved.
The main target groups are youth, women, persons with disability and minority groups in seven so called conflict clusters around Bor, Wau, Aweil, Bentiu, Malakal, Torit and Rumbek. Behaviour and attitudes at communal level will be changed through strengthening of capacity and increased participation of these groups in decision making and other key processes.
PaCC II is a broad, comprehensive project that aims at strengthening the coherence between humanitarian, development and peace efforts, i.e. the triple nexus. The project includes support for prevention, mediation and peacebuilding and early recovery, with a view to decreasing the risk of violent conflict and crises that generate humanitarian needs and undermine development.
The total budget of the four-year project is 35 MUSD, or approximately 315 MSEK. The proposed contribution from Sida is 120 MSEK over the four year period, from June 2020 to March 2024. It constitutes about 33 % of the total budget. Other contributing donors are Japan, KOICA (South Korea) and the African Development Bank.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution Peace and Community Cohesion Project in South Sudan, phase II
Beslut om ändring av insats PaCC II
Financing Agreement between Sweden, represented by Sida, and UNDP on the Peace and Community Cohesion Project in South Sudan, Phase II

description.narrative: PaCC II has rolled out smoothly and the overall progress towards project output is good. Examples of results achieved within the PaCC II project during the first half year of operation, June to November 2020, includes: - The establishment of 14 Payam and one county level Peace Committees; 219 (whereof 31 percent women) Peace Committee members are trained in Transformational Leadership, Conflict Management and GBV. - 107 cases of SGBV were resolved by community psychosocial support groups; cases were taken to court, and the survivors were given psychosocial concelling and other medical services. Tension created between the clans of the perpetrators and the survivors were in many cases solved through mediation. - Enhanced capacity of 133 women leaders for effective participation in local governance and peace processes (in Aweil, Wau, Bentiu and Juba). - A study on youth subculture was completed, guiding the further engagement of youths within the PaCC project. - Support to High Level committee for investigating the conflict in Jonglei and Pibor (including a field mission to Pibor). The focus on UNSCR 1325 during the course of PaCC II, as well as during the former phase of PaCC, has resulted in increased participation in peace and governance processes of women leaders and young women aspiring to become leaders. During the activity period for PaCC II, young aspiring women leaders have mobilized 70 youth to volunteer in a door-to-door Covid-19 prevention campaign. As a result, the young women have formed the first-ever youth volunteer movement in South Sudan. Based on results from the previous phase, PaCC I, it can be seen that the projects have had a positive impact on cattle related conflicts, which are now more often successfully avoided or de-escalated through the traditional conflict resolution mechanism under the auspices of UNDP's civil society partners. The social economic activities for women, organised within the project, improved both inter-communal relations and the livelihood of the participating women. Furthermore, through coaching and mentorship, youth and persons with disability improved their skills, permitting them to gain greater confidence for participation in peace and governance processes. Although progress towards the objectives are overall good, the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent restrictions on movement have hampered the ability to successfully achieve all set goals for 2020. The deteriorating security situation in some of the targeted areas are further delaying the implementation of activities. In addition, excessive flooding during 2020 delayed the finalisation of some of the activities pertaining to infrastructure. UNDP identifies a number of lessons learned, including the importance of engaging youth and the use community radios to promote peace, prevent Covid-19 and countering hate. Furthermore, UNDP identifies the use of arts and sports as an efficient method for strengthening the social cohesion among youth. During 2021, UNDP envisages that the project will strengthen efforts to reduce community and small arms violence, re-integrate ex-combatants as well as dealing with other underlying causes for conflict such as cattle raiding. Youth, peace and security will be another area of focus.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published

title.narrative: Responding to Food Insecurity in South Sudan through Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Frontline and Pipeline

description.narrative:
The project seeks to address food insecurity in South Sudan, by providing life-saving assistance focused on increasing access to safe, equitable and dignified access to WASH services to host communities, internal displaced populations (IDPs) and returnees, in critically affected areas. IOM’s WASH Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPnR) teams will improve access to WASH services to underserved and vulnerable populations in areas classified as IPC 4 and 5, expecting to target 73,500 direct beneficiaries (19,404 women, 19,183 men, 21,022 girls, 13,891 boys) in Tonj East (Paweng, Makuach, Paliang), Tonj South (Tonj payam, Thiet, Jak), and Tonj North (Manlor, Pagol, Aliek, Alabek, Marial Lou). Other payams are currently not accessible due to ongoing intercommunal conflicts. Final selection will be in line with WASH Cluster EPampR TWG Guidance.
IOM will ensure provision of safe water through borehole rehabilitation, including nutrition sites and with access for people with disability. IOM will also ensure the sustainability of water supply through the training of pump mechanics and the provision of spare parts for ongoing care and maintenance of boreholes. Jointly with Nutrition partners, IOM will conduct training and provision of WASH NFIs to SAM caretakers to promote water treatment and safe handling at household level. IOM will additionally promote good hygiene practices through hygiene promotion activities and distribution of basic household hygiene items, including provision of menstrual hygiene kits for women and girls of menstrual age to support menstruation management with dignity. Additionally it will contribute to mitigating WASH-related GBV. Community consultation and safety audit will be conducted prior to any intervention (the rehabilitation, drilling of boreholes, WASH NFI distribution) to ensure safety and security are considered to mitigate any risk of violence. In partnership with Nutrition partners (World Vision, CCM), the project is also designed to reach severe acute malnourished children's caregivers, while ensuring inclusiveness of people with disabilities (PWD) and ensuring that GBV and protection are mainstreamed.
IOM Core Pipeline will procure and release key WASH NFI humanitarian relief items to support the immediate provision of in-kind support for WASH responses in prioritized locations in Tonj East, Tonj North, and Tonj South in Warrap State, as well as WASH Cluster prioritized counties in Jonglei and Lakes States, to alleviate targeted households’ suffering as the result of both severe food insecurity and flooding. Items to be released for partner’s integrated response include hygiene materials such as soap, hygiene kits and/or menstrual hygiene kits targeting the SAM caregiver families, and household water treatment products and storages..

title.narrative: Provision of S-NFI pipeline supplies to Cluster partners, and NFI assistance for beneficiaries in South Sudan

description.narrative: IOM co-leads the Shelter and Non-Food Items (S-NFI) Cluster and manages 100 per cent of the core common pipeline. This project is focused on procurement, transportation and prepositioning of Shelter/Non-Food Items (NFIs) materials for the common pipeline in South Sudan. IOM is responsible for procurement, warehousing and transportation of pipeline stocks and partners are responsible for assessment and distribution of these stocks. The project will enable IOM to procure 25,700 NFI kits and 4,110 shelter reinforcement kits. The project also responds to the needs of vulnerable communities in remote areas who are unable to access nearby markets due to conflict and logistical challenges, and need support for resilience building activities such as cash-based interventions (CBIs). Humanitarian needs for S-NFI remain high across many parts of South Sudan. Currently, it is predicted that the pipeline stock levels will deplete towards the end of the year. In order to fill the gap, IOM as the pipeline management agency will procure NFIs such as mosquito nets, kitchen sets and blankets, and shelter materials such as bamboo in the second quarter of the project to transport and preposition for partner responses. Stocks will be transported to key locations for timely interventions to address lifesaving humanitarian needs. The availability of sufficient and prepositioned stocks in prioritized locations will improve S-NFI partners’ access to critical emergency supplies that will allow them to provide timely lifesaving services to most vulnerable populations. Kits will be prioritized for mobile responses across Jonglei, Upper Nile, Unity, Eastern Equatoria, Northern Bahr El Ghazal and Warrup while providing flexibility to respond to emerging needs in other areas of South Sudan. The South Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SSHF) funding will prevent any disruption of lifesaving supplies and enable Cluster partners to distribute vital S-NFI kits to communities remaining in dire need.

title.narrative: Integrated Education and Protection (GBV CP) Response for People Affected by Conflict and Flood in Ezo and Leer (Envelope 2 3)

description.narrative:
The projects seek to support a total of 12,665 (1,538 W, 1,236 M, 4,866 B amp 5,025 G) internally displaced people in Ezo (Western Equatorial State) and Leer (Unity State) through an integrated education and protection, Gender base violence (GBV) amp child protection (CP), response. A total of 6,940 displaced people in Ezo and 5,725 displaced people in Leer will benefit from this intervention. The project will promote access to quality, protective and inclusive education to 6,820 children (3410 G 3410 B) aged 3 to 18 in Ezo while also guarantying capacity building to 120 (75 M amp 45 W) on school management committee. The project will also support flood affected community in Leer through integrated GBV and CP comprehensive case management services targeting 352 (165 G, 131 B, 50 W, amp 6 M) displaced people. Furthermore, through a community-based approach 5,373 affected people (1,155 W, 1,443 M, 1,325 B amp 1,450 G) will be reached through GBV and CP risk mitigation and prevention measures to enhance the overall protective environment in Leer. In Ezo, the project will focus on education and seek to improve access to school infrastructure through construction amp rehabilitation of school infrastructure. To guarantee safety, protective access amp reduce the threats of GBV and COVID-19 spread, the project will also construct amp rehabilitate WASH facilities of the school including latrines and handwashing stations. Furthermore, the project will promote children enrollment, reduce school dropout followed by internal displacement through back to school and back to teach campaigns in seven targeted schools (Ezo Central, ECC Masumbu, IDP Baikpa, Wenepaida, Progressive, St. Augustin amp Nanzinga) whereby displaced children are hosted. Secondly, the project seeks to improve the quality of educational services provided in the target schools through two sets of activities. One set of activities aiming at the increasing of managerial skills of teachers and administrative school staff through the provision of training for 120 teachers (75 M and 45 W) on Psychosocial support (PSS), school management training particularly focused at the development of COVID-19 and PSEA protocols tailored to every school context and the distribution of scholastic material to learners. The other set of activities aims at strengthening the protective environment of children in the schools and includes the establishment and strengthening of child clubs and school committees composed of parents, teachers and community leaders to guarantee community ownership of the project.
In Leer, the project will focus to holistically respond to flood displaced people protection need through comprehensive GBV and CP case management at WGFS/CFS complemented by community based GBV and CP risk mitigation and prevention measures in Leer town and Kai-ga. Additionally, a strong focus will be put in establishing women amp child friendly mechanisms to guarantee beneficiaries including children are able to voice their concerns in an appropriate manner. Finally, the protection component will support directly 2,020 people at risk (461 M, 738 W, 331 B and 490 G) through GBV response while a total of 3,705 people at risk (700 M, 775 W, 1125 B amp 1125 G) through child protection responses. Particular focus will be given to women and children having suffered the major consequences of internal displacement due to flood. Children having engaged in child labor, force marriage, amp UASC will be supported through the provision of individualized case management services including FTR and referral services. PSS will be guaranteed for all GBV survivors and children in WGFS/CFS which will be fully equipped. The wider community will be sensitized on the main GBV and CP concerns occurring in the IDP settlement location. It is expected that through the conduction of these activities, the overall general environment of women and children hosted in Leer will be improved until a sustainable solution is established.

title.narrative: Security Support to UN and Implementing Partners Operating in South Sudan

description.narrative:
The significant increase in demand for humanitarian agencies to access areas affected by humanitarian crisis and spreading conflict has led to an increased need to conduct ad-hoc security risk assessments (SRAs) to support access negotiations and take advantage of windows of opportunity to deliver critical humanitarian assistance. The project will create a humanitarian security team supervised by the Deputy CSA (Operations) that services the prioritized needs outlined in the humanitarian strategic response plan - with a focus on security risk assessments (SRAs), briefings and advisories. Additional funding is requested for flight hours for a dedicated security aircraft to permit DSS the flexible deployment of security personnel to conduct SRAs, and to provide rapid security support and response, including complementing UNHAS capacity for staff relocations and medical evacuations.
The joint UNDP/UNDSS and WFP/UNHAS proposal (14-RR-UDP-001 / 14-RR-WFP-002) aims to provide dedicated security support for humanitarian operations in South Sudan from January to June 2014. UNDSS will deploy two field security coordination officers and hire one national database operator and administrative assistant to bolster DSS services in South Sudan. WFP will contract and operate a plane dedicated to DSS security and risk assessment missions. DSS expects to carry out 120 missions (requiring 540 flight hours) over the six-month implementation period.

title.narrative: PROTECTING HOUSING, LAND AND PROPERTY RIGHTS IN TRANSITION (PHLAPRIT)

description.narrative: This project contributes to addressing protection issues regarding Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights including illicit occupation of HLP, limited knowledge of legal protection of HLP rights of IDPs, HLP based communal conflict, limited provision of legal information, counseling and lack of sustainable and innovative community based HLP dispute resolution mechanisms. Therefore, this project seeks to strengthen protection programming and mitigate risks from consequences of conflict or displacement. These will be achieved through (1) mapping of HLP issues (including illicit occupation of displaced persons housing and land, host community and IDPs land dispute and existing mechanisms for HLP disputes resolution), (2) Raising awareness on HLP and the law, on spot monitoring and response to assist IDPs reclaim their land and properties, provision of free legal aid and (4) Establishment of innovative and sustainable community based alternative dispute resolution mechanism.Due to the complex nature of HLP issues and limited information on HLP issues in the project locations, the SSLS intends to carry out assessment, establish innovative and sustainable community mediation groups and provide continuous legal aid services. This interventions require a period of at least nine (9) months to implement and coordinate HLP program.

title.narrative: Envelope 2: CCCM, Health and MHPSS, S-NFI, and WASH Response to Support People to People in Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Sites

description.narrative: According to the 2021 South Sudan Humanitarian Needs Overview, most displaced people are expected to remain displaced in 2021, and Bentiu and Naivasha internally displaced persons (IDP) sites and Malakal Protection of Civilian site (PoC) will continue to be refuge for a significant number of IDPs as subnational violence, fragile peace, and a lack of basic services persist in South Sudan. The Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) priority for this allocation is to continue providing camp management services and site care and maintenance. Under the health sector, IOM is contributing to improve people’s access to and utilization of essential healthcare services. Within these efforts, and in line with the priority for integrated quality essential health care services, IOM is providing focused, non-specialized mental health and psychosocial services at the sites. Additionally, IOM continues to coordinate and provide shelter-non-food Item service depending on the needs of the community, as well as integrated, safe, equitable, and dignified access to water, sanitation and hygiene services to IDPs.

title.narrative: South Sudan - Emergency Water, Sanitation, Nutrition and Protection Assistance - World Vision 2019
Soudan du Sud -Aide d'urgence en eau, assainissement, nutrition et protection - Vision Mondiale 2019

description.narrative: With GAC’s support, World Vision Canada is providing emergency water, sanitation, hygiene, nutrition and protection assistance for up to 118,306 conflict-affected people in South Sudan’s Upper Nile state. Project activities include: (1) supporting 9 water treatment systems and rehabilitating waterpoints in 10 targeted schools; (2) supporting community-based management of acute malnutrition; (3) providing messaging on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) best practices to 28,181 pregnant and lactating women, 7,500 women of childbearing age and 5,500 men; and (4) reaching 12,000 women, men, boys and girls with gender-based violence services and referral information.

Mars 2019 - On estime que 7,1 millions de personnes dans le Soudan du Sud ont besoin d'aide humanitaire et de protection dans tout le pays en raison du conflit armé, de l'insécurité alimentaire, de la malnutrition, du déclin économique et des maladies. Environ 1,9 million de personnes sont déplacées à l'intérieur du Soudan du Sud et près de 2,3 millions de Soudanais du Sud ont cherché refuge dans les pays voisins. On estime que 6,2 millions de personnes souffrent actuellement d'une grave insécurité alimentaire et que les taux de malnutrition dépassent les seuils d'urgence. Les épidémies de maladies transmissibles ont mis à rude épreuve un système de santé déjà débordé. L'accès humanitaire reste limité dans de nombreuses régions et un grand nombre de personnes ne sont accessibles que par largage. Avec l'appui d'AMC, Vision Mondiale Canada fournit une aide d'urgence en matière d'eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène, de nutrition et de protection à 118 306 personnes touchées par le conflit dans l'État du Haut-Nil au Soudan du Sud. Les activités du projet comprennent : 1) appuyer 9 systèmes de traitement de l'eau et réhabiliter des points d'eau dans 10 écoles ciblées ; 2) appuyer la gestion communautaire de la malnutrition aiguë ; 3) diffusion de messages sur les meilleures pratiques d'alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant à 28 181 femmes enceintes et allaitantes, 7 500 femmes en âge de procréer et 5 500 hommes ; 4) fourniture de services et de références sur la violence fondée sur le genre à 12 000 femmes, hommes, garçons et filles.

title.narrative: 2017 SS019 SS4002 Community based Child Protection and Psychosocial Support through Capacity Strengthening of National NGOs and direct services to select communities in South Sudan

description.narrative: Conflict and Consequence: As a result of the last three years of armed conflict, more than 3 million people in South Sudan have been displaced either within country, to Protection of Civilians sites, or to neighboring countries. Community practices and structures for protecting children are severely disrupted in all settings, and children are exposed to multiple sources of extreme vulnerability including direct conflict exposure, separation from caregivers, and the exacerbating effects of conflict on harmful community and familial practices such as child marriage and family violence. Today at least one million children are believed to be in psychological distress in South Sudan . The general population, especially children, are documented as suffering from symptoms associated with psychological distress, post-traumatic stress and depression . As the ongoing violence continues to affect both displaced and host communities, it is essential to strengthen community-based child protection networks which can help mitigate the effects of conflict on children’s psychosocial well-being. At the same time, direct response is needed to address more acute needs for psychosocial and child protection support.

Specific Objectives: 1. At-risk children (including youth) access educational, vocational and psycho-social Support

2. Children and adolescents reached with critical child protection services

Expected Results: 1. Capacity of national NGOs enhanced to deliver quality Child Protection and Psychosocial Support. 2. Children and adolescents have increased access to support and services that address their psychosocial and protection needs, through CFS in Upper Nile (Malakal Town); Jonglei (Bor—Malek and Pariak); Eastern Equatoria (Nimule) services. 3. Effective and continued coordination among emergency PSS actors

title.narrative: Nutrition assistance for relief and recovery supporting transition and enhancing capabilities of vulnerable populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal.

description.narrative:
Malnutrition indicators are high across South Sudan. Over 70 percent of the acutely malnourished Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs) who are in need of treatment for acute malnutrition are in the States which are not directly affected by the current conflict. Northern Bahr el Ghazal has the highest prevalence in country with 39.9% of women being wasted. Under this project, WFP, in coordination with NGO partners, will provide targeted supplementary feeding to 9,725 Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northern Bahr el Ghazal to treat acute malnutrition.
Recognizing women’s physiological vulnerability during pregnancy and lactation, the program will provide a nutritious supplement to acutely malnourished PLWs to ensure they stay healthy during this period. Given the chronic nature of malnutrition in Northern Bar El Ghazal, WFP will leverage Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) to provide nutrition education on infant and young child feeding practices. Moreover, through other sources of funding, WFP will implement complementary interventions to address chronic food insecurity among the targeted population. These interventions include preventative Blanket Supplementary Feeding for children under two years of age as well as for PLWs, as well as Food/Cash Assistance for Assets which helps restoring and enhancing livelihoods and build resilience of targeted communities.
As the sole pipeline provider of the commodities for the treatment of MAM, WFP will preposition strategically during the dry season to ensure timely dispatches of commodities to distribution sites.

description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
Phase 1 of the implementation concerned an in-depth analysis of the AAH South Sudan team and the target community. We conducted multiple surveys to gather information on: • From AAH-SS: understanding of entrepreneurship/business concepts, the level of skills and capacity as trainers and program managers, their support needs. • From target community: the profiles of the potential entrepreneurship participants, the economic sectors in the community, the hurdles faced (by men v women), their support needs. The research among AAH-SS staff was conducted through 1-on-1 interviews by CWW. In total we managed to conduct 5 interviews with over 8 AAH-SS staff and AAH-I staff. The research among the target community was set-up by CWW, but conducted by AAH staff, given the language barrier - the common tongue in their communities is Juba Arabic. We created survey’s to be filled out by the staff who liaise with the local communities. The understanding that we received from the research was that the literacy level was practically non-existent and the communities, our target audience don’t live in villages in close knit groups but are semi-nomadic where they roam the rural areas of South Sudan in the drought and settle during the wet season, mainly on the banks of the river. During this wet season, businesses would spring up and those that had any starting capital could invest in products to sell. Tea shops, small bakeries, phone charging stalls seemed to be the most common types of businesses that would serve as our target audience.
This research informed the 2 elements of the training that CWW and AAHI have developed: the management training and the curriculum training. We created the in person training week to encompass: A 8 to 12 lesson interactive entrepreneurship curriculum for AAH-SS to use in their communities. This curriculum includes presentations, trainer manuals, participant workbooks and everything else needed for AAH-SS to conduct the curriculum. CWW and AAHI have provide training-of-trainers sessions to AAH South Sudan to master this curriculum. A 3 to 5 lesson Management program for AAH-SS staff to become effective program managers and trainers of entrepreneurship programs.
Post training in Nairobi, the curriculum was shared with the AAH-SS staff to be translated into Sudanese Arabic. Right after, a sourcing plan was made to start sourcing the types of cooperatives that could join the ‘Jumpstart’ Programme. However, plans were disrupted with insecurity incidents that resulted from cattle invasion from our project areas of Eastern Equatoria state, the environment couldn't enable conduct of trainings. After closely monitoring the security situation, training was resumed after a small delay. Currently, at project end, we have successfully managed to conduct all required trainings with the cohorts of agri-entrepreneurs and cooperatives in Eastern Equatoria state.

Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. description.narrative: Sydsudan präglas sedan december 2013 av konflikt som särskilt sedan juli 2016 ökat i intensitet och spridning. Landet genomsyras av humanitär kris och stora flyktingströmmar. Projektet Peace and Community Cohesion (PaCC) ämnar att i denna svåra miljö bidra till att reducera konflikter och säkerhetsrisker på lokalsamhällesnivå, genom att investera i initiativ som berör grundorsaker till våldsam konflikt. Projektet kommer att stärka lokalsamhällen att identifiera orsaker och faktorer som driver på konflikter i samhället, genom en inkluderande, deltagande och integrerad ansats som tar hänsyn till jämställdhet och kvinnors, mäns, flickors och pojkars olika behov. Genom att effektivt förebygga, hantera och lösa konflikter på ett icke-våldsamt sätt antas att relationer i lokalsamhällena kommer att stärkas. Projektet kommer att ge stöd i att identifiera och stärka kulturella, sociala och ekonomiska förbindelser (connectors) som bidrar till ökat samarbete och förtroende, under tider av fred och konflikt, och över gränser såsom kön och ålder. Insatsen ska bidra till det mer övergripande målet om stärkta förutsättningar för fred och god samhällsstyrning på nationell och lokal nivå.

South Sudan has been characterized by conflict since December 2013, which has intensified and proliferated especially since July 2016. The country is defined by a humanitarian crisis and major refugee flows. In this difficult environment, the Peace and Community Cohesion project (PaCC) seeks to contribute to the reduction and mitigation of community level conflict and insecurity by investing in initiatives that address key drivers of conflict and insecurity. The project will empower communities to identify in an inclusive and participatory manner, the drivers of conflicts in their communities, and using an integrated and gender sensitive approach taking into account the different needs of women, men, girls and boys. It is assumed that effectively preventing, managing and resolving conflicts in a non-violent manner will strengthen community relationships, by identifying and strengthening cultural, social and economic connectors that make communities reliant on each other in times of peace and conflict, across sex and age divide. This will in turn contribute to strengthened peace and governance.

Intended outcome of the intervention is Peace and governance strengthened, Relationships improved between divided communities and policy frameworks and institutional mechanisms enabled for peaceful and inclusive management of emerging and recurring conflicts and tensions.

The Enhanced Integrated Framework (EIF) is a program-based global partnership involving the Least Developed Countries (LDCs), donors and international organizations, to support LDCs to be more active players in the global trading system by helping them tackle obstacles to trade. In this way, the program works towards a wider goal of promoting economic growth and sustainable development. The EIF consists of 23 donors, 6 multilateral organizations (IMF, ITC, WTO, UNCTAD, UNDP, World Bank), two observers (UNIDO and UNWTO) and 51 countries (48 LDCs and the three countries that recently graduated from the LDC category).
Since 2009 Sida has supported the EIF with 120 MSEK for the implementation of phase 1 that lasts until 2017. Sida is now planning to support EIFs implementation of phase 2 with 100 MSEK over the period 2017-2021. The total of EIFs phase 2 covers the time period of 2016-2022. The intervention’s estimated total budget is 274-320 million USD.
The EIF's purpose remains unchanged in phase 2 and aims at supporting LDCs' own drive to: (1) mainstream trade into national development strategies, (2) set up structures needed to coordinate the delivery of trade-related technical assistance, and (3) build capacity to trade, which also includes addressing critical supply-side constraints.
The focus of the EIF is to build capacity within trade in LDCs and to carry out so-called Diagnostic Trade Integration Studies (DTIS) to understand the traderelated restrictions a country is facing. A country-specific action matrix is then formulated to be able to identify actors and financiers who can implement these actions. In some cases, priority actions are implemented and directly funded within the EIF program. Illustrative examples of such priority actions from phase 1 are for example the High Value Silk Project aimed at increasing the competitiveness of the Cambodian silk sector to create jobs particularly for women, assistance for WTO accession and capacity building activities for key trade support institutions, government officials etc. Furthermore, the EIF aims to strengthen donors' support to a country's trade agenda. LCDs can use the EIF as a vehicle to assist in coordinating donor support and to lever more resources within trade, whereas donors can sign up to the EIF as a vehicle to deliver on their commitments concerning trade. EIF activities are financed through a multi-donor trust fund.
The global EIF management structure consists of an EIF Steering Committee, the EIF Board, the EIF Executive Secretariat and a Trust Fund Manager. The EIF Steering Committee serves as the overall governing body of the EIF whereas the EIF board is the key decision-making body for the EIF program and provides strategic oversight. It is composed of one representative each from the six EIF partner agencies and by three representatives each of LDCs and donors. The EIF Excecutive Secretariat is Sida's implementing partner as well as the operational manager of the EIF program and is housed at WTO headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The UNOPS regional office in Geneva acts as trust fund/financial manager for EIF phase 2 and is Sida's agreement partner.
On the country level a national EIF focal point leads the EIF process in-country, a EIF donor facilitator works with the EIF focal point to facilitate donor coordination and the EIF National Steering Committee is a senior-level forum for decision-making and coordination among government partners on trade, the private sector, civil society and the donor community of the specific country.

Enhanced Integrated Framework (EIF) är ett program-baserat partnerskap som inkluderar de minst utvecklade länder (MUL), givare och internationella organisationer. Målet är att stödja MUL att vara mer aktiva aktörer inom det globala handelssystemet genom att hjälpa dem att minska deras hinder inom handelssektorn. På detta sätt arbetar EIF programmet mot ett övergripande mål för att främja ekonomisk tillväxt och hållbar utveckling. I dagsläget består EIF av 23 givare, 6 multilaterala organisationer (IMF, ITC, WTO, UNCTAD, UNDP, World Bank), 2 observatörer (UNIDO och UNWTO) och 51 länder (48 MUL och 3 länder som nyligen lämnade MUL kategorin).
Sida har gett stöd till EIF sedan 2009. Stödet har uppgått till 120 MSEK för implementering av EIF fas 1 som pågår fram tills 2017. Den föreslagna insatsen innebär att stödja EIF:s implementering av fas 2 med 100 MSEK under åren 2017-2021. Hela tidsperioden av EIF fas 2 omfattar åren 2016-2022 och insatsens totala indikativa budget ligger på 274-320 MUSD.
EIF:s syfte är oförändrat i fas 2 och syftar till att stödja MUL att: (1) integrera handel i nationella utvecklingsstrategier, (2) upprätta de strukturer som krävs för att samordna leveransen av handelsrelaterat tekniskt bistånd, och (3) bygga upp handelskapacitet, vilket även omfattar att ta itu med kritiska begränsningar på utbudssidan.
Fokus inom EIF är kapacitetsuppbyggnad inom handelsfrågor av MUL och framtagande av behovsanalyser, så kallade Diagnostic Trade Integration Studies (DTIS). Därefter tar man fram landspecifika åtgärdsmatriser i syfte att kunna identifiera aktörer och finansiärer som kan genomföra insatserna. I vissa fall implementeras och finansieras prioriterade åtgärder direkt inom ramen för EIF. Exempel på sådana prioriterade åtgärder från fas 1 är "High Value Silk" projektet som syftar till att öka konkurrenskraften hos den kambodjanska silke sektorn för att skapa arbetstillfällen särskilt för kvinnor, stöd för anslutning till WTO och kapacitetsuppbyggnad för handelsinstitutioner, regeringstjänstemän osv. Vidare syftar EIF programmet till att stärka givarnas stöd till landets egen handelsagenda. MUL kan använda EIF som en mekanism för att samordna givarstödet och tillför mer resurser inom deras handelsagenda, medan givarna kan ansluta sig till EIF som en mekanism för att leverera på deras åtaganden inom handelsfrågan. EIF:s aktiviteter finansieras genom en multi-donor trust fund.
EIF:s globala förvaltningsstruktur består av EIF styrkommittén, EIF styrelsen, EIF sekretariatet och en fondförvaltare. EIF:s styrkommitté fungerar som ett övergripande ledningsorgan, medan EIF:s styrelse är det beslutande organet för EIF-programmet och ger strategisk tillsyn. Styrelsen består av en representant från varje multilateral organisation (IMF, ITC, WTO, UNCTAD, UNDP, World Bank), tre representanter från de minst utvecklade länderna och tre representanter från givargruppen. EIF:s sekretariat är den genomförandepartner/operativa förvaltaren av EIF-programmet och är en del av WTO:s huvudkontor i Geneve, Schweiz. UNOPS regionala kontor i Geneve fungerar som fond/finansiell förvaltare för EIF fas 2 och är Sidas avtalspartner.
På landnivå leder en nationell EIF fokalpunkt själva EIF processen i landet, en EIF donor facilitator arbetar tillsammans med EIF fokalpunkten för att underlätta givarsamordningen och EIF:s nationella styrkommitté är ett forum för beslutsfattande och samordning mellan statliga parter inom handel, den privata sektorn, det civila samhället och givarna i det specifika landet.

Objectives of the intervention
The intended outcome of the EIF is to support the LDCs to use trade as a route to poverty reduction and sustainable development by enabling them to be more active players in, and beneficiaries of, the global trading system through mainstreaming trade. By the end of the intervention, the EIF has created a strong, sustainable and effective results-oriented partnership among all EIF stakeholders and provided a framework for trade capacity-building. Moreover, the EIF has provided support in the design and implementation of trade policy, alongside the necessary regulatory reform so that EIF countries own a trade agenda conducive to sustainable pro-poor growth as well as EIF countries have increased their presence in international markets.

description.narrative:
Background
Despite COVID 19 and other challenges persisting in 2021, least developed country (LDC) exports increased by an estimated 22% for the year. This maintains the share of the LDCs in global non-oil exports at 1% of the global total, though sustainably up from 0.5% in 2010. There has been continued and increasing commitment by the LDCs themselves to take a lead role in improving their economic situation, working handin-hand with EIF partners to build institutional and productive capacities, thereby contributing to strengthening their standing in the global trade market and their resilience to national and global shocks and challenges.
The EIF Agencies remain a central pillar for technical assistance to the LDCs (with 20% of all projects implemented directly, and more where EIF Agencies provide specialist services to projects). In total, 75 partners supported EIF Countries globally, including women entrepreneurs, micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprise (MSME) associations and regional development banks. This is aligned with the goal of EIF Phase Two, as well as the global recognition of the importance of cross-sectoral and crossthematic partnerships for effective sustainable development and trade.
The case for enhanced integration of the LDCs into global and regional trade markets continues to gain attention. Over 2021, the EIF's communication and advocacy efforts showed an increase of more than 116,500 new website users. EIF Country partners engaged in more than 88 meetings at the ministerial and expert level, again showcasing the interest, importance, and effectiveness of bringing country expertise and examples into the global policy dialogue. Learning and accountability were strengthened through a participatory programme evaluation.
Hereunder are some examples of concrete results achieved by 2021. The results are illustrated by the major components of the EIF programme.
A) Improved trade environment for inclusive and sustainable growth
1) 15 new trade and investment regulations adopted (59 in total), including the revision of the Investment Code in Comoros and the Decree on Cross-Border Trade in Equatorial Guinea. 2) 6 new trade- and investmentrelated policies with support from the EIF (52 in total), such as the Trade Policy Document in Guinea and an Intellectual Property policy in Rwanda.
3) 2 additional countries with government-donor dialogue mechanisms (45 in total), with the EIF playing a lead role in the coordination of project support towards Timor-Leste's accession to the WTO.
4) 1 country (Vanuatu) now leading regional indicators for digital and sustainable trade facilitation
B) Increased exports and access to international markets for the LDCs
1) 52 new international market transactions facilitated through EIF support (211 in total), such as dried fruit from Benin to Switzerland, Coffee from the Central African Republic to Nigeria, Cassava from the Solomon Islands to Australia, and honey from Zambia to Norway. USD
2) 210 Millions USD in new exports with contributions from EIF interventions (USD 680 million in total), including products such as cashew nuts from Togo and shea butter from Burkina Faso.
3) 60% of beneficiaries from EIF productive capacity-building projects are women (up from 56% in 2020), with women-centric projects being implemented in countries such as Bangladesh, Bhutan, Haiti, South Sudan, TimorLeste and Uganda.
Around 4,500 new jobs have been created with contributions from EIF projects (36,000 in total), such as horticulture in Lesotho or ecotourism in Comoros.
Sida has contributed in the strengthening of the EIF reporting and monitoring system through a call off agreement which has led to a marked improvement in the EIF capacity in monitoring and evaluating its support to LDCs.
The results achieved by the EIF are in in line with Sida's objectives in the area of trade. The EIF has contributed at both normative and operational levels. It has constributed to institutional strengthening in a number of LDCs.
The EIF programme, phase 2, is planned to be finalised by end of 2024. Sida's last disbursement of 15 MSEK scheduled for 2022 has been postponed to 2023. This postponement will not affect the programme as there are enough cash in UNOPS account which will be carried over to 2023. All the resources are now being used to complete all the ongoing projects, including reporting and evaluation. It is assessed that the objectives of the EIF programme will be met. Important to note that Sida has contributed with additional consultancy support to the EIF in order to strengthen the its RBM system.

title.narrative: Emergency Shelter and NFI support to vulnerable conflict-affected internally displaced communities in Mayendit, Koch and Leer counties, South Sudan

description.narrative:
PAH will provide life-saving ES-NFIs to the most vulnerable newly displaced conflict-affected communities in Mayendit, Koch and Leer counties, South Sudan, targeting 38,000 beneficiaries displaced due to the ongoing conflict in these areas. The emergency shelter and NFI intervention is meant to save lives and reduce the suffering of the communities targeted. This will be done through supporting people who will mostly already be receiving a multiplicity of other assistance such food assistance, FSL, health, WASH and nutrition to assist them live dignified lives and also re-build their lives in the face the famine and emergency food insecurity affecting the areas where they are seeking temporary shelter.
The activities will be conducted by the PAH Emergency Response Team (ERT) comprised of ES/NFIs specialists with 3 teams of 2 staff each (1 male and 1 female staff) supervised by a Project Coordinator. In order to successfully and rapidly conduct responses, the three teams are deployable to three locations at once. The team will implement the project activities by conducting needs assessments, verification/registrations, preparing and carrying out distributions with demonstration on the use of items distributed e.g. mosquito nets and proper use of plastic sheets. 4 PAH MampE Officers and the MampE Coordinator will independently conduct all PDM surveys and share the outcomes with the team and cluster partners. PAH will involve the beneficiaries at all the stages of the intervention cycle to provide a response best suited for the needs of the particular communities served, taking into account vulnerabilities of each represented group: men, women, boys and girls.
Strong focus will be on ensuring that the most sensitive groups (e.g. persons with disabilities, pregnant and lactating women, and unaccompanied elders/minors) in the community will be served appropriately to their needs and in the manner not exposing them to additional stress and harm. The safety, security and protection needs of the targeted communities will be given particular attention in planning assessments, focus group discussions, verifications/registrations, distributions and pot-distribution monitoring, including in designing and implementing a complaints response mechanism for each intervention.
Due to the insecurity in other locations, PAH can recommend survival kits for distribution working with the local authorities and partners on the ground. In most of the targeted locations, PAH will work closely with WASH partners (including the PAH EP and R team) to ensure that the WASH and Emergency Shelter and NFIs are coordinated as they will be targeting the same beneficiaries (Currently, the locations where survival kits will be recommended are not known, the same with the number of beneficiaries that will be targeted for survival kits. These locations and the number of beneficiaries will only be known after an assessment and registration is done depending on the context on the ground when the programme starts). PAH may also provide added capacity for any form of distributions for other health, FSL and nutrition partners on the ground if they have less capacity and the PAH ES-NFI team will be on the ground.
The response will be coordinated with the S-NFI cluster at national and state levels in order to ensure that PAH is answering to the priority needs and gaps in response capacity in the four focal areas, and any other locations as may be highlighted by the cluster coordination team and the State and Site Focal Points. Assessment, registration/verification, distribution/intervention and post-distribution monitoring reports will be shared with the site, state, cluster coordinators and cluster partners. This will enhance the efficient use of cluster capacity, ensure gaps are effectively filled, needs addressed and lessons are shared to improve future interventions and to contribute towards the revision of the ES-NFI implementation strategy.

title.narrative: (MA) Emergency response survey, clearance and risk education for conflict affected populations in Wau and Jur River Counties

description.narrative:
DDG will deploy a Multi-Task Team capable of conducting survey, clearance and risk education (RE) to enhance safety and freedom of movement across Wau and Jur River Counties, Western Bahr el Ghazal state. Tasks which will support the multi-sector humanitarian response in the area will be prioritised. Capacity on the ground will consist of one combined roving Multi-Task Team (MTT) capable of conducting Battle Area Clearance (BAC), Manual Mine Clearance (MMC), Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD), Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Risk Education (RE). The MTT team will be structured and equipped such that it will have the capacity to split into two separate EOD sub-teams that can operate independently of each other, with the Team Leader and Deputy Team leader managing operations of each of the sub-teams, overseen by the Technical Field Manager (TFM). Both EOD sub-teams will be staffed by a dedicated medic and equipped with two vehicles.
The activities proposed under this project are further elaborated below:
NTS – to target and prioritise clearance according to humanitarian need, survey will be conducted using a mixture of key informant interviews and household questionnaires held with the local population and authorities. NTS will determine the likely locations and density of Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) contamination in target locations, whilst assessing the impact of these hazards on vulnerable populations in any given location. MMC / BAC - the MTT will be able to act as a MMC / BAC capacity, performing static clearance activities across larger, clearly defined areas (identified through the above data collection activities and technical survey as appropriate). EOD – once NTS has determined the nature of the threat, technical capacities within the team will be deployed to remove and destroy identified hazards. The MTT can split its technical capacity into two separate EOD sub-teams to adopt a more flexible, mobile approach that can address explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) spot tasks, as well as limiting staff exposure to security risks by remaining highly mobile. RE – the team will contain a capacity to deliver safety messaging raising awareness amongst at-risk population groups about how to recognise dangerous items, as well as associated safe practices that should be followed, and high risk behaviour that should be avoided in relation to ERW.
DDG has extensive experience operating in Wau, on which it will draw in the implementation of this project. Immediately upon the project commencing, DDG’s MTT will be deployed to Wau Town, where a light base camp will be established and training/accreditation will commence. The MTT will primarily be comprised of existing DDG staff in order to avoid delays relating to recruitment, and assets currently on standby (including 4 Landcruisers - 2 of which will serve as safety vehicles - and a UNIMOG truck) will be moved to Wau to enable the team MTT to rapidly commence activities. Though based out of Wau Town, the team will be highly mobile, roving across Wau and Jur River Counties, both of which remain highly contaminated and have sizable IDP populations.
As the project start date will be in the wet season, locations in Wau and Jur River Counties that are accessible from Wau Town will be prioritised in the early stages of the project. Several such areas remain heavily contaminated with cluster munitions and other ERW, which pose an imminent and significant risk to IDPs and Host Community living or transiting through in these locations. In the dry season, activities will begin in locations further from Wau Town with high rates of contamination. DDG will continue tracking the broader humanitarian response in Wau and Jur River Counties as well as contextual developments that lead to changes in civilian population movements, in order to ensure that areas of operations are prioritised based on continuously evolving civilian and humanitarian needs in the target counties.

title.narrative: Emergency Support to Improve Livelihoods in Upper Nile State
Soutien d’urgence pour améliorer les moyens de subsistance dans l’État du Haut-Nil

description.narrative: This project supports the short-term food needs of approximately 66,000 people (of which 60-70 % are women and children) in both displaced and host communities in Paniykang, Malakal, Nasir, Melut, Longochuk and Ulang counties of Upper Nile State, some of the most conflict-affected areas of South Sudan. The project distributes emergency livelihood kits, which include such items as farming tools, fishing equipment, cooking stoves and animal vaccines. The kits are designed to encourage large-scale emergency food production, protect agricultural related livelihoods and help reduce the level of food aid required to keep people alive during this critical period. The project also intends to provide training to ensure that the kit materials are used properly.

Ce projet permet de répondre aux besoins alimentaires à court terme d’environ 66 000 personnes (de 60 % à 70 % de femmes et d’enfants) de collectivités déplacées et de collectivités d’accueil dans les comtés de Paniykang, de Malakal, de Nasir, de Melut, de Longechuk et d’Ulang, qui font partie de l’État du Haut-Nil et qui comptent parmi les régions les plus touchées par le conflit au Soudan du Sud. Dans le cadre du projet, on distribue des trousses d’urgence pour protéger les moyens de subsistance. Ces trousses contiennent des outils agricoles, du matériel de pêche, des appareils de cuisson et des vaccins pour les animaux. Elles visent à favoriser la production alimentaire d’urgence à grande échelle, à protéger les moyens de subsistance liés à l’agriculture et à contribuer à réduire la quantité d’aide alimentaire requise pour que ces populations survivent durant cette période cruciale. De la formation sera également donnée pour que le matériel que les trousses renferment soit utilisé convenablement.

title.narrative: Emergency Health, Water and Sanitation in South Sudan - CARE Canada 2013
Assistance d'urgence en santé, eau, et assainissement au Soudan du Sud - CARE Canada 2013

description.narrative: March 2013 - Ongoing inter-ethnic, militia and cross-border conflicts in South Sudan continue to create significant displacement, resulting in increased pressure on water and sanitation infrastructure, as well as the health infrastructure throughout the country. With Canada's support, CARE Canada will provide emergency healthcare, water, sanitation and hygiene to 75,500 returnees, internally displaced persons, and host communities in Rubkhona County, Unity State, South Sudan. Project activities will focus on: supporting three primary health centres through outpatient services; distributing essential drugs and supplies; providing training on health education and supervising home visits; establishing 20 new clean water points and rehabilitating 30 existing water points; constructing emergency latrines for newly displaced; and training 200 people on health and hygiene education.

Mars 2013 - Les conflits interethniques, entre milices et transfrontaliers qui sévissent actuellent au Soudan du Sud continuent d'entraîner des déplacements importants, ce qui comme conséquence, d'augmenter la pression sur les systèmes d'approvisionnement en eau et d'assainissement, de même que sur les établissements de santé dans l'ensemble du pays. Grâce au soutien du Canada, CARE Canada fournira des soins de santé d'urgence, des services d'approvisionnement en eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène à 75 500 rapatriés, personnes déplacées à l'intérieur de leur propre pays ainsi qu’aux collectivités d’accueil dans le comté de Rubkona, dans l’État d’Unité, au Soudan du Sud. Les activités du projet viseront à: soutenir trois centres de soins de santé primaires par l’entremise de services de consultations externes; distribuer des fournitures et des médicaments essentiels; donner une formation sur l'éducation en matière de santé et à superviser les visites à domicile; créer 20 points d'eau potable et en remettre 30 en état; construire des latrines d'urgence pour les personnes nouvellement déplacées à l'intérieur de leur propre pays; et donner à 200 personnes une formation sur l'éducation en matière de santé et d'hygiène.

title.narrative: Provision of Emergency Lifesaving WASH interventions focusing on Prevention of Cholera Outbreak in Yirol East county of Lake States, South Sudan

description.narrative:
Cholera outbreaks struck Yirol East county at a point when the county was witnessing unprecedented heavy rainfall where over 2,864 cholera cases and 69 cumulative deaths (CFR-2.4%) were reported at week 24 of 2017. There are mounting fears that the outbreak could strike in different parts of Yirol East,
The aim of this project is to reduce morbidity and mortality from Cholera Outbreak by providing essential Lifesaving WASH interventions to vulnerable people living in Machar-Achiek, Shambe Port ,and Mamer area of Yirol East.
LiveWell will improve access and scale up WASH activities that reach out to the 25,000 vulnerable and conflict-affected populations with: Hygiene promotions and educations activities to 13,500 households (reaching out to at least 25,000 conflict-affected people). Cholera Awareness campaigns at community level reaching out to over 25,000 people. Demonstrate and distribute the WASH supplies to the households and the public settings reaching out to 25,000 people, Conduct community meeting to strengthen and build the capacity of 24 local community leaders as Cholera Focal Persons. Rehabilitate or construct 2 toilets and 2 hand-washing facilities at the 2 ORPs that LiveWell will establish in Yirol East county.

description.narrative:
MSB (the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency) is a Swedish agency tasked with providing and supporting humanitarian operations and interventions. This agreement sets out the Humanitarian Framework for all humanitarian contributions financed by Sida's Humanitarian Unit in which MSB is the Swedish government agency providing operative capacity to humanitarian interventions, through contributions in the form of secondments, the establishment of humanitarian base camps and shelters, medical teams etc in support of UN Organizations. In addition, MSB complement their humanitarian work through their own contributions in capacity development projects in connection with the establishment of rescue services.
Sida and MSB has worked closely together within the framework for swedish humanitarian assistance since 2006 and this partnership has previously shown good results, in particular with regards to MSB’s ability to provide operational and technical assistance to humanitarian actors in both protracted and sudden onset emergencies. The UN agencies are the most common benefactor of such surge deployments and secondments. In addition, MSB has constructed base camps in Nigeria to improve access and seconded personnel to improve emergency response planning in Iraq.
MSB’s interventions and contributions consist of surge deployments, secondment of technical expertise, construction of base camps and material support to humanitarian actors, based on demands. For each calendar year, MSB develop an annual strategic plan in accordance with this agreement, to guide their humanitarian work, which is submitted and approved by Sida. This agreement was initially signed for a three-year period (2018-2020) but was later extended by 1 year to cover the period 2018-2021, with a total allocation of 450 MSEK from Sida to MSB.

Myndigheten för Samhällsskydd och Beredskap (MSB) är en svensk myndighet som i enlighet med sin instruktion ska kunna medverka med insatser i Sveriges internationella humanitära verksamhet. Detta innebär att MSB är den svenska myndighet som operativt bidrar till effektiv humanitär respons på plats genom att de har kapacitet att snabbt svara upp mot behov som uppstått hos humanitära aktörer i fält via sin surgekapacitet. Insatserna omfattar exempelvis sekonderingar, basläger, medicinska team och minröjning.
Sida har samarbetat med MSB och den tidigare myndigheten Räddningsverket inom ramen för det humanitära biståndet sedan 2006. Under föregående överenskommelse har MSB visat på god resultatuppfyllelse samt bedömts av Sida spela en relevant roll i det humanitära biståndet genom dess möjlighet att bidra till humanitära organisationers kapacitet att svara upp mot hastigt förändrade eller förvärrade behov i kriser och konflikter. Exempelvis genom etablerandet av basläger i Nigeria för ökad humanitär närvaro och sekonderad personal för att stärka arbetet med responsplanering i Irak. Traditionellt sker samarbetet till stor del med FN organisationer.
Insatser med MSB innefattar personellt och materiellt stöd till humanitära organisationer baserat på deras efterfrågan. MSB definierar i sin årsplan den strategiska inriktningen för respektive år vilken godkänns av Sida. Överenskommelsen var ursprunglig treårig (2018-2020) men förlängdes senare med ett år för att täcka perioden 2018-2021 och omfattar totalt 450 MSEK.

Målet med insatsen är: Rädda liv, lindra nöd, skydda egendom och värna miljö, främja frihet och säkerhet samt stärka motståndskraft mot kriser och katastrofer i samhället. MSBs resultatramverk specificerar förväntad outcome och intermediate outcomes per effektområde. För respektive effektområde är förväntad outcome följande: - Hantering: Kris- och katastrofhantering är behovsbaserad, effektiv och samordnad. - Återhämtning: Kris- och katastrofhantering integrerar återinrättandet av centrala samhällsfunktioner och återhämtande förmåga. - Resiliens: Effektiv hantering av kris- och katastrofrisker stärker resiliens i samhället.

description.narrative:
Under 2021 genomförde MSB totalt 78 humanitära insatser inom ramen för den fleråriga överenskommelsen mellan Sidas enhet för humanitärt bistånd och MSB (2018-2021). Likt tidigare år har huvuddelen av MSB:s humanitära insatsverksamhet, mätt i antalet insatser, skett inom effektområdet hantering som ska bidra till att kris-och katastrofhantering är behovsbaserad, effektiv och samordnad. MSB stödjer ansvariga aktörer, vars resurser inte räcker till, med expertis och resurser för en mer effektiv hantering, bland annat i form av sekundering av personal till humanitära organisationer för stärka deras förmåga att leda och samordna krisinsatser, inom en rad tematiska områden (operativa leveranser).
Under 2021 påbörjades totalt 41 nya insatser inom effektområdet hantering, jämfört med 36 under föregående period. Inga nya insatser påbörjades inom effektområdet återhämtning, och en ny insats inom jämställdhet och resiliens påbörjades under 2021 med delfinansiering från andra medel, likt tre andra insatser inom effektområdet som pågick sedan tidigare i Somalia, Uganda, Etiopien och Kenya. Det högre antalet nystartade insatser under 2021 återspeglar faktumet att MSB lyckats anpassa sin verksamhet efter de förändrade omständigheter som uppstått till följd av coronapandemin, bland annat i form av reserestriktioner, skärpta visumkrav och karantänsregler. Arbetsformer och erfarenheter från 2020 förbättrade MSB:s möjligheter att leverera resultat trots gällande corona-restriktioner och merparten av MSB:s insatspersonal kunde återgå till arbete i fält, vilket stärkte förutsättningarna för goda resultat jämfört med olika former av distansarbetslösningar. Genom det resultatramverk som MSB tog fram i dialog med Sida under 2019 kan resultatuppfyllnad per insats och operativ leverans nu enklare följas över tid, och detta resultatramverk har varit ett välkommet instrument att använda i kölvattnet coronapandemin och de förändrade förutsättningarna som rådde på grund av coronapandemin. Den övergripande resultatuppfyllelsen är högre under 2021 jämfört med 2020 och Sida delar MSB:s bedömning om att en återhämtning var väntad till följd av att pandemins konsekvenser för insatsverksamheten successivt avtagit. Analysen av MSB:s resultatindikatorer påvisar inga markanta skillnader vad gäller resultatuppfyllelse mellan de olika tematiska områden, de så kallade operativa leveranserna (OL). Sida gör därtill bedömningen att det finns förutsättningar för ytterligare stärkta resultat under 2022, då pandemins påverkan på insatsverksamheten bedöms ha minskat ytterligare, grundat på en kontinuerlig dialog med MSB samt att MSB vid årsmötet med Sida i september 2022 indikerat att de kan skönja ytterligare förbättringar vad gäller resultatuppfyllelse under 2022.
En överväldigande majoritet av insatsverksamheten under 2021 har genomförts i linje med de på förhand fastställda geografiska prioriteringarna som återfinns i de årsplaner MSB årligen lämnar in till Sida. De största mottagarländerna under 2021, sett till antalet nya insatser, var Sudan (6 insatser), Etiopien (5 insatser) och Haiti (4 insatser). Haiti var däremot inte en på förhand fastställd geografisk prioritering men beslut om insatser till Haiti togs efter att landet drabbats av en rad naturkatastrofer.
Huvuddelen av MSB:s nystartade insatser under 2021 (19 av 41 nystartade insatser) skedde inom den operativa leveransen om att stärka humanitära aktörers förmåga att leda och samverka, bland annat genom insatser där personal arbetat med ICT, informationshantering, behovsbedömningar och samordning. Ett sådant exempel är en insats i Tchad, där MSB säkerställde att det fanns fungerade ICT-infrastruktur, nätverk och rutiner på plats hos alla IOM:s kontor för att säkerställa en välfungerande och säker kommunikation och informationshantering, och på så sätt möjliggöra en behovsbaserad humanitär verksamhet hos IOM som arbetar med migranter. Ett annat exempel är MSB:s insatser i Haiti, i samband med en jordbävning och tropisk storm i augusti 2021, där MSB:s insatspersonal bidrog till EU:s civilskyddsmekanisms arbete med att genomföra behovsbedömningar och samordna det humanitära responsarbetet i landet. Inom ramen för denna insats stöttade MSB även EU:s team med boende-, ICT- och kontorslösningar, säkerhetsbedömningar, samt vissa logistiska och administrativa uppgifter för att säkerställa att insatspersonal kunde fokusera på sina huvuduppgifter inom behovsbedömning och samordning. MSB genomförde därtill ytterligare insatser i Haiti där de försåg den jordbävningsdrabbade befolkningen med tillfälliga boenden i form av 200 familjetält och andra större tältlösningar för att säkerställa att undervisning och viss sjukvård kunde fortsätta efter att infrastrukturen skadats i samband med jordbävningen.
Under 2021 fortsatte MSB med sitt arbete med att stärka ansvariga aktörers kapacitet inom jämställdhet och att förebygga könsbaserat våld, vilket väl i linje med Sidas strategi för humanitärt bistånd och prioriteringen att systematiskt integrera skyddsarbete i den globala humanitära responsen för att minska skyddsrisker och våld. En rad insatser genomfördes under året till stöd för UNICEF, WFP, UNFPA och UN Women i länder så som Sudan, Etiopien, Mali och Sydsudan. Genom sin insatsverksamhet har MSB bidragit till att säkerställa att preventiva åtgärder vidtas inom det humanitära responsarbetet för att minska risken för könsbaserat våld och för att stärka kapaciteten hos dessa aktörer och lokala institutioner att bistå de kvinnor och barn som utsatts för våld. Därtill har MSB inom ramen för detta arbete även bidragit till att öka kvinnors och flickors inflytande över det humanitära responsarbetet genom att verka för stärkt kvinnligt deltagande under utformning-, genomförande- och uppföljningsfasen. Ett gott exempel på detta är från Sudan där MSB:s expert inom könsbaserat våld kartlade skyddsrisker och humanitära behov, identifierade lokala aktörer för att stärka deras förmåga att arbeta förebyggande genom att ta fram tydliga arbetsrutiner, samt genom att öka medvetenheten hos olika grupper inom den drabbade befolkningen vad gäller skyddsfrågor och kvinnor och barns rättigheter, bland annat genom befintliga ungdomsaktiviteter.
Under 2021 har MSB även arbetat med att färdigställa en rad större boende-, logistik- och kontorsinsatser för att möjliggöra humanitär närvaro och verksamhet i svårtillgängliga områden i Demokratiska republiken Kongo (DRK), Sydsudan och Centralafrikanska republiken (CAR). Därtill byggde MSB även fyra stycken tillfälliga humanitära hubbar på gränsen mellan Sudan och Etiopien för att stärka den humanitära närvaron och förutsättningarna för UNHCR och andra humanitära aktörer att effektivt bistå de människor som flydde konflikten i Tigray, Etiopien. Vid dessa boende- och kontorslösningar, så kallade humanitära hubbar, kan personal från humanitära organisationer övernatta och arbeta ifrån för att på så sätt möjliggöra kontinuerlig närvaro och en stärkt förmåga att nå ut till krisdrabbad befolkning i svåråtkomliga områden där säkerhet, stora avstånd och bristfällig infrastruktur annars försvårar det humanitära arbetet. Genom dessa insatser bidrar MSB med förbättrade förutsättningar för humanitära aktörer att nå ut med livräddande insatser till drabbad befolkning genom att möjliggöra tillträde och utökad verksamhet. Flera större och permanenta hubbar färdigställdes under 2021 och har lämnats över till både WFP och IOM, bland annat i Kananga, Demokratiska republiken Kongo, där WFP och andra humanitära aktörer tack vare MSB:s har kunnat etablera en starkare närvaro i området och på så sätt säkerställa en mer effektiv humanitär respons. Preliminär data från 2022 visar att det i snitt sker 218 övernattningar på hubben i Kananga per månad, och att det på tre nyligen färdigställda hubbar i Sydsudan också sker hundratals övernattningar per månad bland medarbetare från 20 till 50 humanitära organisationer, beroende på hubb.
