description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

Final conclusions TMT+/TMT (in case of final report) Reflect on how the training has contributed to addressing the capacity needs as described by the requesting organisation in the proposal form. How effective and efficient has the TMT+ been in reaching the desired objectives? Please formulate lessons learned and recommendations for the post-project period.
+
In your email submitting the final report, the partners will enclose: - an inventory of equipment purchased - a document signed by the (Lead partner) Dutch consortium/provider and Lead partner consortium country A or requesting organisation on the transfer of ownership - a list with the names and email addresses of staff members who participated in staff training for their registration in the Holland Alumni Network database

actual.value:
As this training was a Refresher Course mostly for OKP/NFP alumni from courses organized by Ecopolis, the capacity needs assessment for the training was based on Ecopolis' previous experience with the trainees. The training deepened the alumni's understanding of the important role that businesspeople fulfill in their communities, and the challenges they are facing in providing the crucial economic services in the remote IDP settlements. These challenges are partly a result of the way that donors, (I)NGOs and TVET providers perceive and act towards private IDP entrepreneurs. The alumni and Ecopolis conducted a critical analysis of current IDP Relief and Reconstruction programmes, in which many ineffective projects were found due to limited pre-study, follow-up and needs assessments. The next step was to respond to these findings by developing and testing, in collaboration with two groups of private IDP entrepreneurs, strategies and methods to improve their professional skills and business conditions. Together with the target group, a sustainable support system was set up through a structural mentoring programme, the constitution of VSLAs, and opening the possibility of access to loans by opening a bank account for the VSLA and even the realistic possibility of Agent Banking for the town-based banks like Stanbic.
Both Ecopolis and its alumni consider the training to have been effective in reaching its objectives. The alumni and Ecopolis re-established and strengthened their relationship and willingness to assist each other. The alumni also built a strong relationship with the two pilot groups of IDP entrepreneurs in the settlements, which can form the basis for sustainable future collaboration and expansion of support to IDP entrepreneurs in other zones. The strategies and methods set up during the training practically support the crucially important move from Relief to Reconstruction, and from dependence to self-reliance. The solutions developed during the training, for instance the mentoring programme and the self-governing VSLAs with access to loans, take into account the mobile character of the target group, and have the potential to remain well-functioning support systems even when international IDP support moves on to different locations.
The closing public workshop of this refresher course, allowed the alumni , as well as representatives of the IDP entrepreneur target group to exchange and discuss with relevant stakeholders in IDP development, like local and national government, (international) NGOs, business training providers and IDP organizations. Furthermore, after the refresher course's closure, Ecopolis will -together with the alumni- continue to provide supports especially coaching of the trained local mentors for IDP entrepreneurs. Also, from early 2022, every 3 months the alumni and organizations participating in the last public workshop will organize 'Briefing Discussions" on ongoing IDP business development initiatives, activities, outcomes.
​
**Lessons learned and recommendations for the post-project period**
- It's important to realise that -in terms of meaningful target group organization-just 'setting up a VSLA and opening a bank account' is not a silver bullet solution that works the same in every context. It should be acknowledged (and embraced) that each group is unique, and therefore requires its unique approach. Therefore, a programme like this should not immediately be rolled out and focus on quantitative indicators to measure project success. It's better to keep it small, and set up truly sustainable groups that will provide economic services for both the IDP and host community in the future, than to set up 20 VSLAs of which none would remain after the project support ends. - Extra attention should be given to upcoming IDP based NGOs/CBOs. South Sudanese IDP (youth) groups have in recent years transformed from target group to co-implementers of reconciliation, to grass-roots subcontractors in IDP target group facilitation and support, and -indeed- to competitors of the Juba and Kampala-based regular professional implementers of IDP livelihood and reconstruction activities. Other than that these groups have more affinity with the 'target group' and understand their challenges and opportunities better, they are also more likely to continue supporting them in the future, when interest of international organisation may move on to other locations. - When setting up a continuous mentoring programme with mentors from within the community, it is important that there is someone that these mentors can approach when they run into challenges. In short, the mentors should also have access to advisors providing continuous mentor coaching. They could also serve as the bridge between these advisors and the VSLA they are part of, when the VSLA or constituent members run into problems or have identified relevant training needs. - In developing support, training and coaching for IDP target groups, it should be born in mind that these are in principle mobile groups. They eventually move back to their home villages, or, (as would be probably be the case with the majority of South Sudanese refugees in Northern Uganda), to other places in Uganda that provide better conditions for developing their livelihoods. If they do so, "checking out as an IDP" in UNHCR terms , it does not mean that they do not need any support anymore. Providers of IDP training and business support should therefore find ways of connecting to groups and individuals in stead of locations. This refresher course has taken up that issue and developed some remedial approaches. Future periodical monitoring and periodical discussion of the results with relevant stakeholders -as agreed in the final public workshop of the refresher course- should facilitate the absorption of the new IDP support methods into the policies and programs of the mainstream international IDP support organizations.
​

title.narrative: Assessment of Sustainability and Targeting of DFID’s Water and Sanitation Portfolio, 2011-2015

description.narrative: The purpose of this assessment is to generate quality evidence about the outcomes of DFID’s water and sanitation portfolio (2011-2015), assessing the sustainability of the water supply and sanitation services we have supported, and how effective our programmes have been in targeting poor and vulnerable people. The assessment is made up of two consecutive components – a quantitative assessment of continued use of services based on a representative survey, and a qualitative assessment designed to investigate underlying factors relating to sustainability and targeting. Prior to undertaking the quantitative assessment, the supplier will confirm the availability of results data.

The assessment will fulfil a commitment made by DFID to the International Development Committee (IDC) to establish whether the water supply and sanitation facilities established with DFID support between 2011 and 2015 are still being used. The assessment addresses specific recommendations made by the International Committee on Aid Impact (ICAI) in its 2016 review of DFID’s work in water supply and sanitation. The findings of the assessment will be used to inform on-going and future DFID programming.

title.narrative: Emergency Health Care in South Sudan - Doctors without Borders 2012
Soins d'urgence au Soudan du Sud - Médecins Sans Frontières 2012

description.narrative: With CIDA support, Doctors without Borders (MSF) is helping to provide access to emergency medical care in two areas that have been badly affected by past and ongoing conflicts - the Abyei region of Sudan and Jonglei State, South Sudan. Overall, MSF expects to assist more than 133,000 people over the span of this project, 93,000 in Jonglei and 40,000 in Agok. Project activities will focus on: providing maternal and child health and vaccination services (3,000 first antenatal visits and 69,000 outpatients); providing quality health care to target populations; responding to medical needs arising from conflict; treating infectious diseases in 1,104 conflict-affected beneficiaries; and providing treatment for 2,000 malnourished children. Emergency stocks of drugs and medical supplies will also be maintained.

Grâce au soutien de l'ACDI, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) aide à assurer l'accès aux soins médicaux d'urgence dans deux régions lourdement touchées par les conflits en cours ou passés: la région d'Abyei au Soudan et l'État de Jonglei au Soudan du Sud. Dans l’ensemble, MSF compte venir en aide à plus de 133 000 personnes dans le cadre de ce projet : 93 000 personnes dans l’État de Jonglei et 40 000 à Agok. Les activités du projet sont axées sur: la prestation de services de vaccination et de soins de santé aux mères et aux enfants (3 000 visites prénatales initiales et 69 000 consultations externes); la prestation de soins de santé de qualité aux populations visées; la satisfaction des besoins médicaux découlant du conflit; le traitement de maladies infectieuses au profit de 1 104 bénéficiaires touchés par le conflit; et, l’administration de traitements à 2 000 enfants souffrant de malnutrition. Des réserves de médicaments et de fournitures médicales d’urgence seront également constituées.

title.narrative: Multi-Sectoral Response to Acute Humanitarian Needs of Flood-Affected Population and Those At-Risk of Disease Outbreak in Bentiu IDP Camp

description.narrative: In response to the time critical needs highlighted in the South Sudan Humanitarian Fund First Reserve Allocation - Strategy Paper, IOM is implementing a multi-sectoral and life-saving response to the acute humanitarian needs of people displaced due to conflict in Tambura County and flooding in targeted locations, as well as internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Bentiu Camp at risk of disease outbreak, particularly Hepatitis E. This project is leveraging IOM’s existing presence in Bentiu IDP Camp, as well as its role as Camp Manager and active participation in all relevant coordination forums, whilst also capitalizing upon the capacity of the Organization to rapidly mobilize shelter/non-food item (S-NFI) teams in hard-to-reach locations. Finally, the S-NFI and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) Pipelines will enable IOM to efficiently support lifesaving frontline responses, by ensuring the reliable, cost-effective and steady stream of core relief supplies to partners for distribution to crisis-affected populations in Bentiu IDP site, and conflict- and flood-affected counties across the country.

title.narrative: Enhancing the provision of critical life saving assistance and child protection services to 10 ,600 conflict affected boys and girls, in Mayendit and Panyinjiar Counties

description.narrative: Unity State is one of the most affected States by the current crisis in South Sudan, that has resulted in people being forcibly displaced from their homes, majority, who are now living in UNMISS Protection of Civilians Sites (POC) or moved to other safer places, where they are housed by host communities as IDPs. The conflict has led to breakdown in social structures, schools closed down, a few opened but the attendance of pupils is too low associated with insecurity. Lack of salary to teachers has affected the education system as teachers have resorted to other means of survival. Children have become vulnerable to various types of violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect and are also at risk of injuries, disability, physical and sexual violence as well as psychosocial and mental disorders, even losing their lives. Southern Unity State is only accessed by air during rainy session and the present situation has worsened the transport as movement by road is more prone to attacks. This has led to few basic commodities available on the market being very expensive In responding to the above mentioned needs, UNIDOR is proposing to provide critical lifesaving child protection services to conflict affected boys and girls in Mayendit and Panyinjiar Counties. The proposed six months’ emergency intervention is designed to: i) Increase boys, girls and women access to lifesaving comprehensive case management, family tracing and reunification (FTR) and psycho-social support (PSS) services and child protection services to reduce risks of protection. ii) Integrate child protection monitoring and mainstreaming into the protection intervention to improve the overall context analysis and integration of child protection principles in the intervention that will be scaled up to respond to the identified needs. iii) Enhance understanding and analysis among humanitarian actors on the child protection context and needs. UNIDOR will utilize existing internal emergency response capacity to staff these teams to provide timely, effective and efficient child protection and protection response in Southern Unity. This will offer an opportunity to provide much needed humanitarian services in areas without protection services. This child protection intervention has been especially designed to be integrated within UNIDOR’s already existing child protection program in Payinjiar and Mayendit counties. The project will focus on strengthening Community- Based Child Protection Networks (CBCPN) and facilitating access to information and appropriate services. These CBCPN will support children’s well-being through local structures or traditional ways, while acting both as response to child protection concerns and as prevention, by helping communities reduce risks and better protect children from violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation. In addition, the CBCPN will identify and refer vulnerable children in need of individual support. Adolescents and youth will be engaged in providing peer support, recreational activities and referrals to the FSL programming as an entry point to develop future intervention with Children Associated with Armed Forced/Groups. UNIDOR already has an existing coordinated intervention with VSF Suisse and Germany, in which UNIDOR identifies children informally released from Armed Forces/Groups and VSF provides reintegration and economic recovery interventions, in the form of vocational training. The project will be field focused, child centered and will be family and community driven. Being a National Organisation, 90% of UNIDOR staff are South Sudanese nationals who are well conversant with the environment, weather, traditions , cultures, and the political aspects in Unity State and this offers a distinct advantage when it comes to provision of continued services and interventions even when the area is relatively insecure as the staff move with communities.

title.narrative: South Sudan - Emergency Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Nutrition - Concern Worldwide 2016
Soudan du Sud - Aide d'urgence en eau, assainissement, hygiène et nutrition - Concern Worldwide 2016

description.narrative: March 2016 - In 2016, an estimated 8.7 million people across South Sudan are affected by the effects of armed conflict and inter-communal violence, economic decline, disease, and climatic shocks. Nearly 1.7 million are internally displaced within South Sudan and over 640,000 South Sudanese have sought protection in neighbouring countries. The civil war, as well as erratic rainfall in some areas, has driven 3.9 million people into severe food insecurity, with malnutrition rates over emergency thresholds. Outbreaks of cholera, measles, and hepatitis E have strained an already overwhelmed health system. Humanitarian access remains restricted in many conflict areas and large numbers of people are accessible only by air drops. With GAC 's support, Concern Worldwide is helping to improve health and living conditions for up to 77,028 vulnerable internally displaced and vulnerable conflict-affected people in Unity State and Central Equatoria State, South Sudan. Project activities include: (1) constructing 20 new water points and rehabilitating two boreholes for 38,000 people in the Bentiu Protection of Civilians site and providing a community water point in Bentiu Town; (2) constructing 450 communal latrines benefitting up to 9,000 people and providing hygiene promotion training; (3) providing temporary shelter materials to 600 households and providing 3,000 relief kits; and (4) constructing or rehabilitating eight nutrition centers, and providing supplemental feeding to improve malnutrition in children under five and in pregnant and lactating women.

Mars 2016 - En 2016, on estime à 8,7 millions le nombre de personnes au Sud-Soudan qui seront touchées par les effets du conflit armé et de la violence intercommunautaire, le déclin économique, les maladies et les chocs climatiques. Près de 1,7 million de personnes sont déplacées à l'intérieur du Sud-Soudan et plus de 640 000 Sud-Soudanais ont cherché une protection dans les pays voisins. La guerre civile, ainsi que des précipitations irrégulières dans certaines régions, ont plongé 3,9 millions de personnes dans une grave insécurité alimentaire, avec des taux de malnutrition dépassant les seuils d'urgence. Les épidémies de choléra, de rougeole et d'hépatite E ont mis à rude épreuve un système de santé déjà surchargé. L'accès humanitaire reste limité dans de nombreuses zones de conflit et un grand nombre de personnes ne sont accessibles que par largage aérien. Avec le soutien d'AMC, Concern Worldwide contribue à améliorer la santé et les conditions de vie de 77 028 personnes vulnérables déplacées à l'intérieur du pays et touchées par le conflit dans l'État d'Unity et l'État d'Equatoria central, au Sud-Soudan. Les activités du projet comprennent : 1) la construction de 20 nouveaux points d'eau et la réhabilitation de deux forages pour 38 000 personnes dans le site de protection des civils de Bentiu et la mise en place d'un point d'eau communautaire dans la ville de Bentiu; 2) la construction de 450 latrines communautaires bénéficiant à 9 000 personnes et la formation à la promotion de l'hygiène; 3) fourniture de matériaux pour abris temporaires à 600 ménages et fourniture de 3 000 kits de secours; 4) construction ou réhabilitation de huit centres de nutrition, et fourniture d'une alimentation complémentaire pour améliorer la malnutrition des enfants de moins de cinq ans et des femmes enceintes et allaitantes.

Le résultat ultime escompté est : des vies sauvées, la souffrance atténuée et la dignité humaine préservée dans les pays qui font face à une crise humanitaire ou à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë.

title.narrative: The Gavi Health System Strengthening Programme of the Government of South Sudan

description.narrative: Since the country’s independence in 2011, the protracted conflict in South Sudan has left the country’s health system fragile and unable to address the growing and diverse needs of its population, including that of women and children with very poor and limited infrastructure which remain largely inaccessible to most of the population, including nearly 2 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). This situation is exacerbated by flooding during the six-month rainy season and a severe lack of human resources for health (qualified health care workers). Thus, the country has not been able to meet maternal, new-born and child health care needs, including those related to immunization reflecting a low routine immunization coverage with only 60 percent of children aged under 1 being reported as having received the Penta3 vaccination in 2020, a slight increase from 2019 at 44%. IOM, through the Health Systems strengthening support to the ministry of Health project aims to contribute to increased routine immunization coverage of children 0 to 23 months through scaling up of vaccination services to IDPs, returnees, conflict affected host communities in hard -to-reach locations by strengthening vaccine last mile delivery, service delivery and improved data management.

description.narrative:
Sida´s support to the Health Pooled Fund 3 (HPF3) in South Sudan amounts to SEK 300 million over a period of 3 years (2019-2021) including provision of health services to 8 out of 10 former states in South Sudan. Sida has previously contributed to the fund's Phase 1 and Phase 2 during the years 2012-2018 amounting a total of SEK 299 million.
The fund was designed in 2012 as a multi-donor fund managed by DFID and with presently includes Sweden, Canada and the US.
HPF3 supports delivery of essential primary health care in the community and through a network of health care facilities, secondary health care and referral health services. In addition it supports the stabilisation of local health systems and the strengthening of community ownership and governance structures. Finally HPF3 is responsible for the procurement and supply chain management of essential medical commodities.
HPF3 programme impact will be an improved health and nutrition status for the population that saves lives and reduces morbidity (including maternal, infant and under-5 mortality), and has the following three principal outcomes:
- Improved health and nutrition services for the population, especially women and children. - Improved community engagement and accountability of health services. - Stabilisation of local health systems.
The recipients of services are primarily the state run health services in South Sudan. The direct beneficiaries are the South Sudanese people, with particular focus on mothers, pregnant women and children under five years of age.
Sida believes that HPF3 takes into account the poor peoples´ perspective as one of the objectives of the program is to address extreme poverty. HPF3 integrates the principle of non-discrimination as the services offered are available to the entire population in the geographical areas where HPF3 is implemented. A new focus within HPF3 is to design the program to be adapted to the specific needs of people living with disabilities and who are utilising the program's services. Sida believes that HPF3 has an integrated gender equality perspective with several measurable goals. HPF3 has dedicated staff only to work to support, monitor, and evaluate implementing partners' capacity to integrate gender equality throughout the program cycle. However, Sida believes that this work can be further improved and will work for the programm to undertake a renewed and in-depth gender equality analysis to ensure that the program addresses the shortcomings identified in the analysis.
The implementation takes place in close collaboration with civil society organizations and health authorities at a decentralized level. Due to previous years of prevailing conflict and the limited capacity and resources of the South Sudanese government, the initial focus of the programme has shifted from health system strengthening approaches such as building systems for procurement and distribution of drugs, personnel and financial systems, to the implementation of health services, partly due to a flexible approach and according to humanitarian principles required by the situation. Despite major challenges and due to a flexible programme approach, the HPF has shown good results both in phase 1 and 2.

Insatsen omfattar stöd med totalt 300 MSEK till den tredje fasen av Health Pooled Fund (HPF3) under åren 2019-2021. Sida har tidigare bidragit till fondens fas 1 och fas 2 under åren 2012-2018 med totalt 299 MSEK. Stödet för HPF3 är en ökning i aktivitetsperiod samt beloppsvolym vilket finner sin förklaring i de stora medelsbehoven inom fonden direkt kopplat till de stora behoven av hälsoservice i Sydsudan. Sida bedömer det möjligt att bidra till dessa behov genom dels en längre aktivitetsperiod samt en ökad finansieringen, jämfört med Sidas tidigare stöd till HPF. Utrymme för detta ges iom den förlängda strategiperioden (5 år) samt det ökade anslaget som beslutats om inom ramen för strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Sydsudan 2018-2022. Under första årets budget av HPF3 kommer Sidas uppgå till 13% men andelen kan minskas om EU beslutar sig för att bidra till HPF3. Under 2021 kommer DFID att utvärdera programmet. Utvärderingen skall vägleda ett beslut huruvida programmet skall forsätta i samma konstellation programperioden ut eller alternativt söka en sammanslagning med Världsbankens program som implementeras i de två delstater där HPF3 inte är verksamt. Bereonde på utkomsten kommer Sida avseende eventuellt framtida stöd att bedöma behovet om eventuell förlänging av aktivitesperioden och medelstillskjutning till det forsatta programmet alternativt stödja det nya programmet.
HPF utformades 2012 som en givargemensam fond som leds av DFID och där andra givare till fonden i nuläget är Sverige, Kanada och USA. HPF3´s program är utformat i enlighet med antagna nationella hälsopolicies, framför allt "BasicPackage for Health and Nutrition Services", "Health Sector Development Plan" och "Health Sector Strategic Plan".
DFID har i enlighet med EUs upphandlingregler, upphandlat en fondförvaltare för HPF3. Fondförvaltaren för HPF3 är Crown Agents. Crown Agents är ett internationellt privat icke-vinstdrivande företag som arbetar i utvecklingsländer med att bla stärkande av hälso- och utbildningssystem samt inom humanitära sektorn. Crown Agents arbetar i över 100 länder och kunderna är framför allt multinationella företag, regeringar, FN och biståndsgivare såsom EU, DFID, Världsbanken och Kanada.
Inom HPF3 är Crown Agents ansvarig för genomförandet av HPF3 under ledning av DFID. Crown Agents i sin tur leder ett konsortium som består av ytterligare tre (3) eniteter som bidrar med sin expertiskunskap inom bl.a. områden som upphandling, forskning relaterat till HPF3 programmet och logistik.
Crown Agents kallar till givarmöten för HPF3 månadsvis. Vid dessa möten redogörs för programmets utgifter och en reviderad budget presenteras. Utöver budgetfrågan tas andra aktuella frågor upp löpande och givarna har möjlighet att förslå agendapunkter samt göra inspel till agendapunkterna. HPF3 har även en styrkommitté som håller möten 4 gånger om året. Styrkommittén leds av representant från hälsoministeriet, vanligtvis statssekreteraren, tillsammans med DFID. Alla givare är representerade, samt personal från hälsoministeriet och fondförvaltaren. För HPF3 har medlemmar tillkommit med representanter från Världsbankens hälsoprogram, som implementeras i de två delstater där HPF3 inte är närvarande, och Världbanksprogrammets implementerande partner, detta i syfte att stärka samordningen mellan de båda programmen. Medlemmarna i styrkommittéens främsta uppgift är att vägleda och bidra i strategiska programbeslut, att bidra till en stärkt samordning inom hälsosektorn och att försäkra att HPF3 programmet är i linje med de nationella hälsopolicies som programmet vilar på. Sida bedömer sin medverkan i styrkommittén av betydelse för insyn och möjlighet att påverka och vägleda strategiska beslut i den rikting som Sida vill se att programmet utformas och utvecklas åt.
Crown Agents upphandlar implementerande partner för genomförandet av aktiviteter. I HPF3 har 13 st implementerande partner upphandlats som täcker 21 geografiskt uppdelade områden. Dessa implementerande partner består av internationella och nationella icke-statliga organsiationer (NGOs). De implementerade partnerna skriver under Terms of Reference där uppdraget tydligt defineras. Alla aktiviteter utövas inom ramen för det nationella hälsosystemets strukturer och organisation och med hjälp av personal anställd av hälsoministeriet. De implementerande partnerna betalar en bonus till ett definerat antal personal som krävs för att utföra uppdraget. Denna bonus är utöver den lön som hälsoministeriets ansvar för att betala månadsvis, men som i praktiken utbetalas väldigt oregelbundet och dessutom utgör en väldigt låg summa. Inga medel inom HPF3 överförs direkt till hälsoministeriet eller andra myndigheter.
HPF3 stödjer grundläggande hälso- och sjukvårdsservice i Sydsudan genom ett nätverk av sjukvårdsinrättningar på framför allt primär men i viss omfattning även sekundär nivå. I tillägg främjar programmet stabiliseringen av det nationella hälso- och sjukvårdssystemet och stärkandet av samhällsägarskap och styrningsstrukturer. Slutligen är Crown Agents ansvarig för upphandling och logistikkedjan av viktiga medicinska produkter så som läkemedel och medicinskt material och utrustning.
På sikt kommer effekten av HPF3 att bli en förbättrad hälso- och näringsstatus hos befolkningen som sparar liv och minskar sjukligheten (inklusive mödra-, spädbarns- och under-5-års dödlighet) och har följande tre huvudresultat:
- Ökat och förbättrat utbud av hälso- och nutritionsservice för Sydsudans befolkning, med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och barn. - Ökat samhällsengagemang och ansvarstagande för hälsovårdstjänster. - Stabilisering av det nationella hälsosystemet.
Mottagare av tjänsterna är främst den statliga sjukvården i Sydsudan. De direkta mottagarna är Sydsudaneser med särskild inriktning på mödrar, gravida kvinnor och barn under fem år.
Sida bedömmer att HPF3 tar i beaktande fattiga människors perspektiv då ett av målen med progammet är att adressera extrem fattigdom. HPF3 integrerar principen om icke-diskriminering då de tjänster som erbjuds finns tillgängliga för hela populationen inom de geografiska områden där HPF3 implementeras. Ett nytillkommet fokus inom HPF3 är att utforma programmet att anpassas till de särskilda behov som finns hos människor med funktionsnedsättning och som söker programmets tjänster. Sida bedömer att HPF3 har ett integrerat jämställdhetsperspektiv med flera mätbara mål. HPF3 har avsatt personal enbart för att arbeta med att stödja, följa upp, och utvärdera implementerande partners kapacitet att integrera jämställdhet genom hela programcykel. Sida anser dock att detta arbete kan förbättras ytterligare och kommer driva frågan om en förnyad och fördjupad jämställhetsanalys för att säkerställa att programmet adresserar de brister som identifierats i analysen.
Genomförandet av HPF3 sker i nära samarbete med de av Crown Agents upphandlade implementerande samarbetspartner (NGOs) samt med myndigheter på decentraliserad nivå. På grund av tidigare år av rådande konflikt samt den sydsudanesiska statens begränsade kapacitet och resurser har det initiala fokuset för programmet skiftat från hälsosystemstärkande ansats som att bygga system för upphandling och distribution av läkemedel, personal och finansiella system, till ett större fokus på genomförande av hälsotjänster, delvis i humanitär form där situationen kräver så. Trots stora utmaningar och tack vare ett flexibelt upplägg har HPF under fas 1 och 2 uppvisat goda resultat.

HPF3 merges two previous health programmes; Health Pooled Fund 2 (HPF2), which provides health care at health facility level, and the Integrated Community Case Management 2 (ICCM2) programme, which provides health care to children under-five within more remote communities. HPF3 is programmed between 2018 and 2023 (5 years). HPF3 supports delivery of essential primary health care in the community and through a network of health care facilities, secondary health care and referral health services. In addition it supports the stabilisation of local health systems and the strengthening of community ownership and governance structures. Finally HPF3 is responsible for the procurement and supply chain management of essential medical commodities. A break point of HPF3 is planned for in 2021 to provide an opportunity to either change the direction or the scale of the programme if this is deemed necessary. The HPF3 sees two options at this break point: the situation in South Sudan has changed dramatically and the conditions for sustainable health system development appear favourable, then funding might not be needed. However this scenario is considered unlikely. More likely is that donors would be more willing to support a World Bank led-trust fund model with greater government ownership. HPF3 supports services in eight out of ten hubs of South Sudan in the states formerly known as: Central Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, Lakes, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Warrap, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria. The two remaining former states, Jonglei and Upper Nile, are being funded by a World Bank funded programme and implemented by ICRC and UNICEF as contracted partners. The overall HPF3 programme impact will be an improved health and nutrition status for the population that saves lives and reduces morbidity (including maternal, infant and under-5 mortality), and has the following three principal outcomes: -Improved health and nutrition services for the population, especially women and children. -Improved community engagement and accountability of health services. -Stabilisation of local health systems. The recipients of services are primarily the state run health services in South Sudan. The direct beneficiaries are the South Sudanese people, with particular focus on mothers, pregnant women and children under five years of age. HPF3 will contribute to three of the UN Sustainable Development goals as well as the global programme Scale up Nutrition and the global partnership to empower women and girls by investing in rights-based family planning; FP 2020.

description.narrative: A couple of results on outcome level will be given as examples of good achievements: 1) The proportion of births delivered in a health facility (outcome 1) stood at a national level of 41.8%, while the average for the eight HPF-supported states was higher at 46.7%. This achievement in HPF3 supported states is attributed to increasing number of CEmONC centres and BEmONC centres, Boma Health Initiative activities with health education, sensitisation and community mobilisation and availability of staff. 2) In 2020, survey data was collected for both the proportion of mothers of children 0-11 months who are currently using a modern contraceptive and women 15-49 years who are currently using (or whose partner is using) a modern contraceptive (outcome 2) which stood at 3.0% and 4.3% respectively. HPF3 supported states achieved 3.9% and 5.2% respectively,with significant variation found between states. Challenges faced by the programme due to COVID-19 included delays in drugs and medicines supplies coming into the country and restricted movement from Juba to and between states. To address the meeting and movement restrictions, the programme adapted its programming to be able to conduct online training and meetings. Additionally, HPF3 field office mandates were expanded to cover for the lack of travel by the Juba-based staff. Despite the unexpected changes in the context, the programme was able to adapt and deliver due to the flexibility of the HPF3 team, MoH and IPs.

description.narrative: Port has been implemented by PAX and its local partner since 2015 to promote cross border peaceful coexistence and inter / intra community and tribal peaceful coexistence in three communities, Yirol, Amongpiny (Lakes) and Payinjiar (Unity). The project supports conflict resolution and reconciliation in these communities to leverage changes that can influence the conflict dynamics across the region. Since 2017, the P2P project has also a very specific focus on gender promoting the participation of women in local peacebuilding which is intended to contribute to the implementation of United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 on the community level.

1) Communities of different ethnicity solve their conflicts in a non-violent way and are less receptive of violence instigating propaganda (hate speech, ethnic violence etc.). 2) Communities enjoy good vertical relationships and improved services (security, humanitarian support and development) from local authorities and service providers
Main stakeholder groups in the community, including youth, women, traditional authorities, traders, IDPs and local government

Peace from Below is a program which includes two key projects (APP and P2P). The program supports conflict resolution and reconciliation in the target communities to leverage changes that can positively influence the conflict dynamics across the region and which may then influence the national political / military and ethnic conflict that has devastated South Sudan since December 2013. Peace from Below has also had a very specific focus on gender and the role of women in local peacebuilding which is intended to contribute to the implementation of United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 on the community level.

description.narrative:
The project intends to improve access and scale up responsiveness to essential health care needs of vulnerable populations through PHCU and Mobile team packages in Kajo-Keji County.
This project focus is in line with the SA1 cluster objectives to 1) Improve access and scale-up responsiveness to essential health-care needs of the vulnerable populations by focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality
2) Prevent, detect and respond to epidemic-prone disease outbreaks and promote WASH in health facilities for conflict-affected and vulnerable populations
The main project activities include OPD consultations, emergency measles vaccination for children 6 months-15 years, response to epidemic prone disease alerts within 48 hours, provision of SGBV/CMR services, conduct skilled deliveries at the facility and at home, training of health staff on infection prevention and control (Wash in health facilities) and on disease surveillance and outbreak response, management of children under5 with SAM and medical complications, Social mobilization and health education/promotion for behavioral change.
The project beneficiaries include 20,000 direct beneficiaries, 60% (12,000) IDPS and 10% (2,000) people in the host community. 4% (800) PLW and 26% (5,200) Children lt5 years. By sex, the beneficiaries include 34% (6800) Men, 40% (8,000) Women, 10% (2,000) Boys and 16% (3,200) Girls
This project’s approach is designed to bridge the existing response gaps by increasing population coverage through PHCU and Mobile Teams. 2 PHCUs and 2 Mobile outreach teams will continue to offer services to the needy populations in Kajo Keji. TRI-SS will use the existing MoH reporting tools such as IDSR, EWARS, RRM and Quantified Supervisory check list and the EPI tally sheets and the Health Cluster 5Ws for data collection and reporting. Additionally, The project will use the basic package for health and nutrition services of the Ministry of health (BPHNS), Minimum Initial Service package for Reproductive health services (MISP) and the community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) package and mhGAP, Humanitarian intervention guide (mhGAP-HIG WHO 2015) as working guidelines
To ensure accountability to affected population, 1 inception meeting and 2 community dialogue meetings will be conducted to introduce the community to the project and to provide feedback.
The current coordination mechanisms established with existing partners such as, CHD, RRC and ARC will continue through regular meetings to create conducive working environment and promote corporation.
The already established coordination with Ugandan authorities for security clearance at the border will be strengthened and through its offices in Moyo and Yumbe, TRI-SS will obtain a letter of no objection from the Resident District Commissioner (RDC) to facilitate the movement of supplies including drugs.
Essential drugs will be procured from Uganda Joint Medical store to fill a gap of drug shortages due to restrictions that currently exist in transporting core-pipeline supplies from Juba to Kajo-Keji

title.narrative: Provision of integrated Health and Nutrition interventions for the vulnerable population affected by increased violence, flooding and food security in Canal-Pigi of Jonglei state, and Panyijar of Unity State, South Sudan.

description.narrative:
IMC UK's proposed project will provide critical lifesaving integrated health and nutrition services to the conflict-affected, internally displaced people (IDPs) and host populations in Canal-Pigi and Panyijar Counties in Jonglei and Unity State. The proposed response will reach 22,055 direct beneficiaries (including 2070 men, 9379 women, 5184 boys and 5422 girls) over 12 months in the targeted counties. For nutrition there is 15,968 direct beneficiaries (4273 boys, 4448 girls and 7247 pregnant and lactating women - PLW), including 7,144 for Canal/Pigi and 8823 for Panyjar. The direct number of beneficiaries for health is 14,163 (4815 male, 4957 female, 2,124 boys, 2,267 girls).
The proposed nutrition response will focus on the treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition among children (boys and girls) aged 0-59 months and pregnant and lactating women, through the management of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and moderate acute malnutrition (MAM), as well as provision of Maternal-Infant Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) focusing on the first 1000 days of a child's life in targeted health and nutrition sites. IMC-UK will directly implement nutrition activities in 18 OTP/TSFP/SC sites in Canal-Pigi (8 OTP/TSFP and 1 SC) and Panyijar (9 OTP/TSF). IMC-UK will continuously monitor the nutrition status of the population and the nutrition response through the routine collection and analysis of nutrition program data, mass mid upper arm circumference (MUAC) screening and periodic SMART surveys funded by other donors.
The health activities will be implemented by IMC UK in Canal-Pigi. The health activities will primarily focus on strengthening the capacity of the county health department and health workers in providing integrated quality essential health care services, particularly maternal and child health care including antenatal care, postnatal care basic emergency obstetric care, communicable and non-communicable diseases treatment and surveillance, treatment for injuries and basic first aid, immunization and Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) health education at the facility and community level through BMI using standard IEC and BCC materials provision of essential pharmaceuticals and medical commodities early detection and response to outbreaks and, referral services. IMC UK will deploy one mobile medical team into Alam to ensure the delivery of basic health services.
IMC will ensure MHPSS services are made available for people with mental, neurological and substance use disorders through provision of evidence-based quality mental health and psychosocial support services using WHO-mhGAP-HIG guideline. IMC will integrate psychosocial support into the mobile health team's service delivery, which will target locations within proximity to refer to ECHO-funded facilities supported by IMC. Mental Health officers will take the lead in organizing psychosocial support activities, including PFA, identification and referral of basic needs and mental health case management to effectively offer support to crisis-affected populations. IMC will also work with affected communities to build awareness-raising on stress and anxiety/fear reactions, loss and grief, promotion of positive coping mechanisms, and more. Mental Health Officers will be trained on providing mental health awareness and psychoeducation sessions to communities.
The nutrition and health activities will be integrated, through close coordination and joint programming. The project will further complement and strengthen IMC UK's existing interventions.

title.narrative: Mitigating GBV Risks and Strengthening Life-Saving Response Services for Survivors

description.narrative:
UNICEF plans to strengthen Gender Based Violence (GBV) prevention and response work by supporting other clusters to strengthen GBV prevention and risk mitigation through their sectoral interventions. UNICEF will work closely with the Health and Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) clusters to not only reduce risk of exposure to GBV and prevent it from happening in the first place but also to promote dignity, safety, and participation of women and girls. In addition, capacity building with the Health sector will include life-saving response services, namely clinical management of rape (CMR) training and development of systems for tracking essential CMR drugs, in close coordination with both the GBV sub-cluster and the CMR task force within the RH working group.
The 2015 IASC Guidelines, Integrating Gender Based Violence Interventions in Humanitarian Action, will be used to form the foundation of this work and guide all steps of the process. The guidelines were launched in South Sudan in March 2016. UNICEF, partnering with the WASH Cluster, has led the mainstreaming in WASH interventions in South Sudan and the achievements have been cited globally as best-practice. UNICEF, in partnership with IMC, has already been providing similar support to the Health sector, through a mobile CMR training team.
UNICEF will build on this experience and success, while making use of in-house expertise on GBV prevention and response, to address gaps in CMR coverage throughout the country and support both Health and CCCM to more systematically integrate GBV considerations into their sectoral programming. Activities will take place at national level, as well as field locations of Juba, Yei and Wau, plus additional locations for CMR training to be identified in collaboration with relevant health actors. To keep up with the rapidly changing environment, a mobile CMR training team will be supported to provide trainings to local staff on CMR including administration of essential medicines and care for survivors. This work will be done in close collaboration with the national GBV Sub-Cluster along, state-level GBV working groups (where available), and the Reproductive Health working group. Trainings will be complemented by practical, on-the-ground support to colleagues working in CCCM and Health, including activities like joint monitoring activities (such as safety audits and facility monitoring) and structured action planning. This will seek to strengthen quality of services but also promote and increase system wide accountability for GBV prevention and response in South Sudan.

title.narrative: Food security and Livelihood Emergency project in Yirol East County of Lake State.

description.narrative:
In response to the growing humanitarian crisis in Lake State .WAV Food security and livelihood project will target 34488 vulnerable IDPs and host community beneficiaries from 5748 households in Yirol East county Nyang,Pagarau and Adior Payams .The intervention aims to ensure that lives are saved and human suffering is reduced through provision of emergency main season crop, vegetable and fishing kits for vulnerable households.
The prioritized objectives to achieve the overall goal will include: 1 ) Enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable ,crop and fishing support. 2) Reduce dependency on food and agricultural input to support and strengthen HHs ability to absorb shocks.
The main activities to be carried out to realize this objectives and achieve the overall goal will include :
1) Distribution of agricultural (vegetable seeds) to improve access to food production by targeted IDP and host community individuals – both men and women. 2) Distribution of crop agricultural (crop kits) to improve access to food production by targeted IDP and host community individuals -both men and women. 3) Conduct distribution of fishing kits (hooks and fishing nets)to improve access to food production by targeted IDP and host community individuals – both men and youth.
Several factors have predisposed these targeted IDPs and hot community households to their current food shortages and lack of incomes which include abandonment of their farms due to conflicts, displacements and loss of food stocks and assets. The last proxy indicators show that the coping mechanisms have been stretched to the last limits with decreased daily food consumption. The inter agency assessment report 2018 indicates that women relied on wild food to feed their families while men who support the families through fishing activities have limited fish catches. Women walk for long distances 2-3 days fading for food for their families exposing them to risks. Men who contribute to households incomes through livestock farming has significantly been affected by the recurrent cattle deaths, cattle raiding leading in diminishing of milk production and unfavorable terms of trade since 2016.The reduction in daily meals to one and a times non by most of the targeted vulnerable households has significantly affected lactating mothers which support in breastfeeding. Hence the need to support increasingly vulnerable beneficiaries with access to food production, fishing which is one of the main activities in Yirol East contributes to nutrition and improved households incomes which are constrained due to lack of fishing equipment (hooks and kits.The project intends to provide vegetable,crop and fishing kits and support in extension services to improve production and incomes for 6 months.

description.narrative: In the period 2016-2020, the NIMD country programmes will remain at the heart of NIMD’s work; NIMD is convinced that transformational change processes can only be realised and sustained through country programmes. To inform its programmes, and in particular to design effective strategies that respond to complex and rapidly changing political environments, NIMD will further deepen its knowledge base, invest in its skills-set and develop tools and instruments regarding interparty dialogue, capacity strengthening, political culture, gender equality & inclusion. As part of its knowledge agenda, NIMD will also specifically work on strengthening its strategies, skills and expertise tailored to working in fragile and conflict affected settings in recognition that working in such sensitive contexts requires a tailored approach. Furthermore, to embrace new thinking about participatory democracy and the effect of modern technology on citizens’ engagement in policy and political processes, NIMD will also invest in innovation.

Political actors are defined as the combined main target group of the Strategic Partnership: - (representatives of) political parties - politicians - (Members of) Parliament and its Committees - Other elected representatives at local levels. NIMD will primarily focus on political parties.

The long term outcome defined in the project is to ensure that Security Sector Reforms defined in the peace agreement take into account individual and community security concerns of all South Sudanese in a gender -sensitive manner. Two sub sets of targeted outcomes are clearly defined in the project to achieve the above long term outcome and project impact; a) Capacity strengthening of South Sudanese civil society organisation, b) Policy change through influencing and advocacy. An intended policy change is to ensure that the, implementation of a strategic security assessment, security policy framework, revised defence policy and roadmap for the unification of the army and security forces is based on individual and communities' actual needs and reflects realities at community levels. Focus will primarily be at national level, but also take into consideration the implementation of the peace agreement at local levels. In particular, influencing and advocacy initiatives will focus on the issue of small arms proliferation Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV), high levels of impunity and the presence of local armed groups. title.narrative: Provision of Emergency shelter and Non Food Item to conflict affected People in South Sudan

description.narrative:
WVSS will contribute to the protection of lives of displaced populations by distributing Emergency Shelter and Non Food Items (ES-NFI) to the newly displaced households, protracted IDPs, those in formal IDP site, and the vulnerable households within the host community but are conflict affected. This project, running to February 2018 is designed to complement the ongoing SSHF ES-NFIs project that ends on 31st October 2017, targeting locations which were not targeted in the first standard allocation. All the projects materials for the ES-NFIs will be sourced from the NFI cluster core- pipeline.
The project will focus on counties in the conflict affected states of Jonglei (Uror, Ayod, Nyirol, Duk and Akobo), Upper Nile (Nasir and Maiwut), and Warrap (Tonj North amp South) based on the current trends of displacement. In addition to these, it is noteworthy that WVSS will use its front line Mobile teams to reach hard to reach locations and any locations with ES- NFIs needs within South Sudan, with a greater emphasis on displacement due to conflict.
Where possible the provision of more sustainable and cost-effective non-food items (possibly could also be sourced from local markets).The project will target the most vulnerable households, looking out for any protection issues and referring such to relevant partners. The strengthening of community coping mechanisms and cohesion of vulnerable and at-risk communities will be encouraged.
WVSS will also use its experience in working with National NGOs, especially those new to responding to ES-NFI needs. In past year WVSS has worked with South Sudan Development Agency (SSUDA) and Africa Development Aid (ADA) to implement NFI projects in Upper Nile and Jonglei. By So doing WVSS will be building the capacities of such partners. WVSS will also use its good working relationships in continuation with this collaboration for greater impact and delivery of services to the neediest populations.
WVSS has ongoing operations in the Greater Equatoria Greater Upper Nile and Greater Bhar el- Ghazal states with staff equipped with skills to respond to the needs of conflict affected populations including the undertaking of the needs assessment and ES-NFI distribution. In addition to this, WVSS has teams positioned in strategic static locations Kuajok (Warrap), Yambio (Greater Western Equatoria State), Juba (Central Equatoria) and Melut, Aburoc, Renk and Malakal (Upper Nile). In addition to staff who can respond to any needs in these static Locations, WVSS has two mobile teams based in Juba adding an additional team through this project. The three Mobile teams will be deployed from Juba under the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). The three mobile teams will be competent to respond to ES-NFI needs anywhere in the country especially in locations which are hard to reach as well as carry out the assessments, verification, registrations, and distributions of NFI to the conflict affected groups.
The project will target 40,611 beneficiaries (8,122 households), comprising of 11,777 men, 11,371 women and 17,463 children affected by the conflict. The majority (30,458) of these will be the newly displaced people, while the remaining (10,153) will be from the protracted IDPs and other vulnerable groups within the host community. The priority locations will be, Jonglei, Upper Nile and Warrap States, though the project will have the ability to respond anywhere in the country mainly through its mobile RRM teams.
In order to be able to reach the neediest populations with lifesaving assistance, WVSS will respond to needs requiring immediate multi-cluster, multi- agency response. In such instances WVSS with other agencies and stakeholders will conduct the Inter agency Rapid Needs Assessments (IRNA) to determine the lifesaving needs of the affected populations.

title.narrative: Support to the South Sudan Peace Process
Appui au processus de paix au Soudan du Sud

description.narrative: This project aims to contribute to the peace process in South Sudan by supporting the implementation of the Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (ARCSS) and its oversight mechanism, the Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission. The Commission is mandated to steer South Sudan through the transitional period and ensure the implementation of provisions as described in the Agreement. The four major areas of the Commission’s work include: (1) engaging the Parties to the Agreement, regional guarantors and the international community to establish the conditions necessary to facilitate implementation of the Agreement; (2) monitoring and overseeing the implementation of the Agreement and the mandate and tasks of the Transitional Government of National Unity, including the adherence of the Parties to the agreed timelines and implementation schedule; (3) facilitating the establishment and operationalization of institutions critical for the implementation of the Peace Agreement; and (4) building the capacity of Commission members, relevant actors, other institutions and mechanisms critical for the successful implementation of the peace agreement to effectively monitor the peace process.

Ce projet vise à contribuer au processus de paix au Soudan du Sud en appuyant la mise en œuvre de l’Accord sur le règlement du conflit en République du Soudan du Sud (ARCSS) et son mécanisme de supervision, la Commission mixte de suivi et d'évaluation. La Commission a le mandat de guider le Soudan du Sud durant la période de transition et d’assurer la mise en œuvre des dispositions décrites dans l’Accord. Les quatre grands domaines de travail de la Commission sont les suivants : 1) mobiliser les Parties à l’accord, les garants régionaux et la communauté internationale pour établir les conditions nécessaires pour faciliter la mise ne œuvre de l’Accord; 2) surveiller et superviser la mise en œuvre de l’Accord ainsi que le mandat et les tâches du Gouvernement provisoire d'union nationale, dont le respect par les Parties des échéanciers convenus et du calendrier de mise en œuvre; 3) faciliter l’établissement et la mise en service d’institutions cruciales pour la mise en œuvre de l’Accord de paix; 4) renforcer la capacité des membres de la Commission, des acteurs pertinents, des autres institutions et des mécanismes cruciaux pour la mise en œuvre réussie de l’accord de paix pour surveiller efficacement le processus de paix.

description.narrative: Results achieved as of the end of the project (March 2019) include: (1) the Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (JMEC), the official oversight body on the implementation of the Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (ARCSS) helped shepherd the parties from the failed ARCSS agreement of 2015 to the, so far successful, insofar as South Sudan has not fallen back into widespread conflict, Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (RARCSS) of 2018; (2) overall, JMEC produced numerous reports and updates for all stakeholders, and widely disseminated the agreement; (3) reached a total of 360 people (of which 180 women) , during public outreach campaigns and a further 415 people (of which 455 women), completed training relating to implementing the peace agreement; and (4) overall project implementation enhanced by mainstreaming gender throughout JMEC’s activities, such as gender mainstreaming training and forging strategic partnership with all agreement institutions and mechanisms to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment.

Parmi les résultats obtenus jusqu'à la fin du projet (mars 2019) : 1) la Commission mixte de suivi et d’évaluation, l’organe de surveillance officiel chargé de mettre en œuvre l’Accord sur le règlement du conflit dans la République du Soudan du Sud (ARCSS), a aidé les parties à sortir de l’échec de l’ARCSS de 2015 pour passer à l’ARCSS revitalisé de 2018, qui est un succès jusqu’à présent dans la mesure où le Soudan du Sud n’est pas retombé en situation de conflit généralisé; 2) de façon générale, la Commission a produit de nombreux rapports et mises à jour à l’intention de tous les intervenants et a largement diffusé l’Accord; 3) au total, 360 personnes (dont 180 femmes) ont bénéficié de campagnes de sensibilisation publique et 455 personnes de plus (dont 320 femmes) ont suivi une formation liée à la mise en œuvre de l’accord de paix; 4) la mise en œuvre générale du projet est renforcée par la promotion de l’égalité des genres dans l’ensemble des activités de la Commission, notamment par une formation sur l’intégration de l’égalité des genres et l’établissement d’un partenariat stratégique avec toutes les institutions liées à l’Accord et de mécanismes pour promouvoir l’égalité et le renforcement du pouvoir des femmes.

The expected outcomes for this project include: (1) increased efficiency to monitor and oversee implementation of the ARCSS, the mandate and tasks of the Transitional Government of National Unity and other agreement institutions, including adherence to agreed timelines and implementation schedule; and (2) improved social action by South Sudan citizens and regional and international members to enhance oversight for the implementation of the ARCSS. .

Les résultats escomptés de ce projet comprennent : 1) accroissement de l’efficience pour surveiller et superviser la mise en œuvre de l’ARCSS, le mandat et les tâches du Gouvernement provisoire d'union nationale et d’autres institutions liées à l’Accord, dont le respect des échéanciers convenus et du calendrier de mise en œuvre; 2) amélioration de l’action sociale menée par des citoyens du Soudan du Sud et des membres régionaux et internationaux pour améliorer la supervision de la mise en œuvre de l’ARCSS.

title.narrative: South Sudan Joint Response 1: Supporting the protection and rehabilitation of vulnerable host community, IDPs, and pastoral households’ production assets in Koch and Panyijar (Unity State)

description.narrative: The overall objective of the project is to improve food availability and access to vulnerable households in crisis and emergency phases through the protection and rehabilitation of their crop, vegetable and livestock assets and support in livelihoods. Through the proposed activities, the project will ensure the timely provision of assorted crop seeds—in particular sorghum, maize, cowpeas, and vegetables —and tools, providing beneficiaries with the means to reestablish their own production and help them address the threat of hunger. Other proposed activities include restocking of small ruminant and provision of fishing gear. The project will also provide unconditional cash to the most vulnerable.

The project will target a total of 24,378 direct beneficiaries -4,050 vulnerable households averaging six members per household (6 x 4,050) plus an additional 78 individuals from within vulnerable IDP and host communities in Unity State, in particular Koch and Panyijar Counties.

title.narrative: South Sudan - Water, Sanitation, Hygiene, Nutrition and Protection Assistance - World Vision 2018
Soudan du Sud-Aide en eau, assainissement, hygiène, nutrition et protection - Vision mondiale 2018

description.narrative: As of March 2018, an estimated 7 million people across South Sudan are in need of humanitarian assistance and protection across the country as a result of armed conflict, food insecurity, malnutrition, economic decline, and disease. Approximately 1.9 million people are internally displaced within South Sudan and over 2.4 million South Sudanese have sought protection in neighbouring countries. An estimated 5.1 million people are currently severely food insecure, with malnutrition rates over emergency thresholds. Outbreaks of communicable diseases have strained an already overwhelmed health system. Humanitarian access remains restricted in many conflict areas and large numbers of people are accessible only by air drops. With GAC’s support, World Vision Canada is providing emergency water, sanitation, hygiene, nutrition and protection services for up to 125,916 conflict-affected people in Upper Nile state. Project activities include: (1) rehabilitate the key water and sanitation facilities in 10 targeted schools and 4 health clinics and forming four community water management committees; (2) implementing Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition and screening 13,725 children and 5,779 pregnant and lactating women, and (3) reaching 10,000 women, men, boys and girls with gender-based violence service and referral information.

En mars 2018, on estime que 7 millions de personnes dans le Soudan du Sud ont besoin d'aide humanitaire et de protection dans tout le pays en raison du conflit armé, de l'insécurité alimentaire, de la malnutrition, du déclin économique et des maladies. Environ 1,9 million de personnes sont déplacées et plus de 2,4 millions de Soudanais du Sud ont cherché refuge dans les pays voisins. On estime que 5,1 millions de personnes souffrent actuellement d'une grave insécurité alimentaire et que les taux de malnutrition dépassant les seuils d'urgence. Les épidémies de maladies transmissibles ont mis à rude épreuve un système de santé déjà débordé. L'accès humanitaire reste limité dans de nombreuses zones de conflit et un grand nombre de personnes ne sont accessibles que par largage. Avec l'appui d’AMC, Vision Mondiale Canada fournit des services d'urgence en matière d'eau, d'assainissement, d'hygiène, de nutrition et de protection à près de 125 916 personnes touchées par le conflit dans l'État du Haut-Nil. Les activités du projet comprennent : (1) réhabiliter les installations clés d'approvisionnement en eau et d'assainissement dans 10 écoles ciblées et 4 dispensaires et former quatre comités communautaires de gestion de l'eau ; (2) mettre en œuvre la gestion communautaire de la malnutrition aiguë et dépister 13 725 enfants et 5 779 femmes enceintes et allaitantes, et (3) fournir à 10 000 femmes, hommes, garçons et filles des informations et services en cas de violence liée au genre.
