description.narrative: Sedan 2001 har Sida lämnat stöd till internationella insatser genomförda av Myndigheten för samhällsskydd och beredskap (MSB) och dess föregångare Statens räddningsverk, genom ramöverenskommelser för finansiering av humanitära insatser. Det övergripande målet för MSB:s internationella humanitära verksamhet är att rädda liv, lindra nöd och upprätthålla mänsklig värdighet för katastrofutsatta människor. Detta sker genom sekonderingar till FN-organ, Internationella rödakorskommittén samt internationella NGOs, men även genom MSB:s större insatser inom kontors-, boende- och logistiklösningar. Den nuvarande bidragsöverenskommelsen mellan Sida och MSB löper 2022-2025. MSB är svensk myndighet och dess del i Sidas humanitära biståndsverksamhet skapar förutsättningar för bredare relationer i de länder man verkar och med de organisationer man samarbetar med. MSB omnämns särskilt i strategin för Sveriges humanitära bistånd genom Sida 2021–2025 (UD2020/18531), där vikten av samarbetet mellan Sida och MSB understryks. En betydande del av MSB:s humanitära insatsverksamhet syftar till att möjliggöra humanitärt arbete, och att ge FN-organ och icke-statliga organisationer tillträde till svårtillgängliga områden genom att erbjuda platser att bo och arbeta på. MSB bidrar även med expertis inom en rad tematiska områden och på så vis bidrar man till att stärka upp främst FN-systemet genom sin sekonderingsverksamhet. MSB fyller därmed en viktig roll inom Sidas humanitära portfölj och operationaliseringen av strategin för det humanitära biståndet. Under föregående överenskommelse har MSB visat på god resultatuppfyllelse samt bedömts av Sida spela en relevant roll i det humanitära biståndet genom dess möjlighet att bidra till humanitära organisationers kapacitet att svara upp mot hastigt förändrade eller förvärrade behov i kriser och konflikter. I linje med ambitionen att övergå till flerårigt humanitärt stöd har stöd beslutats om till MSB för de första tre åren av fyraårsperioden, till en total summa på 390 000 000 SEK (130 000 000 per år 2022-2024). Det fjärde årets finansiering kommer baseras på påvisade resultat samt inkommen årsplan för 2025. Geografisk och tematisk inriktning för verksamheten inom MSB:s tre effektområden (Hantering, Återhämtning, Resiliens) varje år specificeras i den årsplan MSB skickar in, där även en övergripande budget ingår. Summan, som är ett genomsnitt av allokeringen de senaste åren (135 MSEK 2020, 125 MSEK 2021), baseras på de stora och ökande humanitära behoven i världen, den stora efterfrågan på insatser från MSB som inneburit att myndigheten behövt göra hårdare prioriteringar under de senaste åren trots anslag som legat högre än åren dessförinnan, samt att MSB byggt upp en kapacitet för att upprätthålla en kvalitativ insatsleverans på den höga nivå som gällt under 2020 och 2021.

The Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB) has since 2001 received funding from Sida through framework agreements for financing of humanitarian operations. The overall objective of MSB’s humanitarian operations is to save lives, alleviate suffering and maintain human dignity for people affected by crisis, conflict and disasters. This is achieved through secondments to UN agencies, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and international NGOs, but also through logistical support and housing and office solutions. The current grant agreement between Sida and MSB covers the period 2022-2025. As a Swedish governmental agency, MSB and its part in Sida’s humanitarian assistance facilitates broader relations in the countries they operate in and with the organizations they cooperate with. A significant part of MSB’s humanitarian operations aims to enable humanitarian activities in hard to reach areas, including by creating the necessary conditions for UN agencies and international NGOs to live, work and operate in those areas through housing and office solutions. MSB also contributes to strengthening the UN system through their thematic expertise by seconding specialists and experts in an array of thematic areas. In the previous agreement period, MSB showcased good results and is deemed to play a relevant role in the operationalization of the Swedish humanitarian assistance strategy. In line with Sida’s ambitions to move towards multi-year funding, MSB is granted funding for three of the four years in the new grant period, amounting to a total of 390 000 000 SEK (130 000 000 SEK per year). The funding for the fourth year will be contingent on results achieved in the first three years and the annual plan submitted for 2025.

Sedan 2001 har Sida lämnat stöd till internationella insatser genomförda av Myndigheten för samhällsskydd och beredskap (MSB) och dess föregångare Statens räddningsverk, genom ramöverenskommelser för finansiering av humanitära insatser. Det övergripande målet för MSB:s internationella humanitära verksamhet är att rädda liv, lindra nöd och upprätthålla mänsklig värdighet för katastrofutsatta människor. Detta sker genom sekonderingar till FN-organ, Internationella rödakorskommittén samt internationella NGOs, men även genom MSB:s större insatser inom kontors-, boende- och logistiklösningar. Den nuvarande bidragsöverenskommelsen mellan Sida och MSB löper 2022-2025.
MSB är svensk myndighet och dess del i Sidas humanitära biståndsverksamhet skapar förutsättningar för bredare relationer i de länder man verkar och med de organisationer man samarbetar med. MSB omnämns särskilt i strategin för Sveriges humanitära bistånd genom Sida 20212025 (UD2020/18531), där vikten av samarbetet mellan Sida och MSB understryks. En betydande del av MSB:s humanitära insatsverksamhet syftar till att möjliggöra humanitärt arbete, och att ge FN-organ och icke-statliga organisationer tillträde till svårtillgängliga områden genom att erbjuda platser att bo och arbeta på. MSB bidrar även med expertis inom en rad tematiska områden och på så vis bidrar man till att stärka upp främst FN-systemet genom sin sekonderingsverksamhet. MSB fyller därmed en viktig roll inom Sidas humanitära portfölj och operationaliseringen av strategin för det humanitära biståndet.
Regeringens övergripande mål för det svenska biståndet är att skapa förutsättningar för bättre levnadsvillkor för människor som lever i fattigdom och förtryck. Målet för Sveriges humanitära bistånd är att rädda liv, lindra nöd och upprätthålla mänsklig värdighet till förmån för nödlidande människor som har utsatts för, eller står under hot att utsättas för, väpnade konflikter, naturkatastrofer eller andra katastrofliknande förhållanden. MSB arbetar som svensk myndighet i sin humanitära biståndsverksamhet för att uppnå dessa mål, och insatsen syftar till att bidra till detta.
Målet med insatsen är att vid insatsens slut ha "räddat liv, lindrat nöd, skyddat egendom, värnat miljö, främjat frihet och säkerhet, samt stärkt motståndskraft mot kriser och katastrofer i samhället". Detta delas i MSB:s resultatramverk in i tre effektområden: Hantering, Återhämtning och Resiliens. Geografisk och tematisk inriktning för verksamheten inom MSB:s tre effektområden varje år specificeras i den årsplan MSB skickar in, där även en övergripande budget ingår. Varje effektområde har delmål (outcomes) kopplade till sig:
1. Hantering Mål: Kris-och katastrofhantering är behovsbaserad, effektiv och samordnad. 2. Återhämtning Mål: Kris- och katastrofhantering integrerar återinrättandet av centrala samhällsfunktioner och återhämtande förmåga. 3. Resiliens Mål: Ökad förmågan hos ansvariga aktörer att integrera hållbar återuppbyggnad i respons och skapa förutsättningar för rehabilitering.

title.narrative: Scale up of Life-Saving Nutrition Interventions in Unity and Greater Equatoria States

description.narrative: The main objective of this joint project with UNICEF is to prevent excess morbidity and mortality in children under 5 years of age and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) due to acute malnutrition. In this joint project, WFP will use CERF funds to procure, preposition and distribute nutrition commodities. A total of 13,668 children and 4,767 PLWs with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) will be treated through one treatment cycle (2 months for children and 5 months for PLWs). Funding will also support additional supplies in especially remote areas, projected to reach 5,000 children under 5. People in Leer, Mayendit, Kajo-Keji, Lainya, Yei will benefit from this support for 6 months.

title.narrative: Setting up skin collection and tannery in South Sudan

description.narrative: The applicant in this project proposal is the Ethiopian registered company Modjo Tannery SC. The local partner is Yabsera Company Ltd. The company is involved in the collection and disposal of solid and liquid waste (sewage water) from companies and government offices.Ethiopia has a vibrant leather industry. As a consequence the competition is fierce and it becomes more and more difficult to collect enough skins for competitive prices. South Sudan has the second biggest livestock population of Africa (after Ethiopia), but the potential of the sector is underutilised. The majority of the skins are thrown away. The project partners see a good opportunity to set up a tannery in South Sudan to produce the wet blue semi-finished product, from sheep and goat skins.The project partners will establish a joint venture. The tannery will be established at the outskirts of Juba.Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)A water treatment plant will be installed according to European standards. Due to the fact that a tannery has a potential risk for environmental pollution and health and safety issues for its employees.1) An extensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) will be conducted by an internationally well-recognised agency with relevant expertise. This EIA should elaborate on the labour conditions, risk of environmental pollution and the construction of an applicable waste water treatment system including a cost calculation of the system.2) If the results of the EIA are unsatisfying and/or the cost of an effective effluent system goes way beyond the reserved budget.3) As there are no laws regarding waste water disposal in South Sudan, nor relevant laboratories to check the water quality, there will be periodic waste water quality controls. The joint venture will sign a long-term agreement with an international recognised laboratory for the quality control of the waste water streams.Impact• Employment and working conditionsThe minimum wages for unskilled labour in South Sudan are not determined, but lower and unskilled staff usually earn around SSD 500 (65 euro). The joint venture will offer at least living wages of 115 euro per month.Other benefits for employees include:- medical care;- protective clothing and work under healthy conditions;- one full meal per day and access to clean drinking water;- free transport will be provided from and to a central pick-up point;- a nurse and medical staff will be hired full-time to provide preventative and curative health care to employees and their family members;- staff will benefit from extensive in-company training programmes.• Innovation / Transfer of knowledgeThere are no tanneries in South Sudan. As mentioned earlier the majority of the skins are just thrown away.• Chain effectsImpact on local suppliersThe raw material (fresh goat and sheep skins) will be purchased from local butchers, farmers and households. With a maximum capacity of 2,000 skins per day, the project will require 600,000 hides per year.The project will set up a system of skin collectors. These collectors work closely with selected contract butchers who, in turn, will be trained to perform the best possible job in the slaughter process to assure the quality of the skins.Impact on local customers or consumersThere will be very little impact on local customers, as the wet blue skins are meant for exports.• Impact on the sectorThe project will set up the first skin processing plant, producing wet blue skins. This will account for new local business initiatives for farmers, butchers and service providers. It is expected that around 20% of the skins offered to the project will be rejected, because these do not meet the required quality standards. To reduce the rejection percentage, the project will organise substantial training to collectors and butchers in order to gradually improve the efficiency and safeguard the market value of the skins.• EnvironmentIn the tanning industry, many different chemicals are used and both solid, liquid and gaseous waste will be produced by the project.The project will implement all necessary measures to mitigate negative effects for the environment, workers health and energy efficiency. An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) will be conducted. A modern effluent treatment plant will be installed according to European standards.• Position of womenSpecial facilities will be available for female workers and staff for personal hygiene and child care. The majority of the workers will be female.
The set-up of a tannery for the production of a semi-finished product called wet blue for the export market. The tannery will have a maximum capacity of 2,000 goat and sheep skins per day.

title.narrative: Life-saving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Services that are Responsive to the Protection needs of Vulnerable Groups at risk of Gender-based Violence (GBV) among the Populations affected by Conflict and Acute Malnutrition in Pariang County.

description.narrative: With a strong community participation, this intervention seeks to deliver increased and improved access to life-saving water, sanitation and hygiene services to the vulnerable populations in Pariang County in a manner that is responsive to their protection needs, especially from gender based violence (GBV) against women and girls. The populations in this area have been prioritized following the recent humanitarian needs assessment for South Sudan 2018 that has identified them among the most affected by conflict, malnutrition and the economic hardship currently experienced in the country among other challenges. To achieve the objectives of this intervention, IAS proposes to address the needs in a twofold approach, namely To re-establish and improve access to water, sanitation and hygiene infrastructure for 15,000 vulnerable people by rehabilitation of non-functional water points on one hand, and to improve the population's health and coping capacity against threats such as preventable water related diseases through increased knowledge of appropriate hygiene and sanitation practices delivered through community training and hygiene promotion activities on the other hand. The intervention will target IDPs, host communities, and under-served communities, in line with CERF life-saving criteria. IAS South Sudan is guided by the Humanitarian Code of Conduct, adheres to the 4 core humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, independence and equality. Furthermore, IAS South Sudan is working towards the application of the Core Humanitarian Standards and is guided by the Sphere minimum standards.

reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title.narrative: Provision of Emergency school meals to affected IDPs and host communities’ vulnerable girls and boys in Unity (Koch, Guit) and Jonglei State (Fangak).

description.narrative:
Crisis affected girls and boys (3-18 years) have access to safe, protective and inclusive learning environments including protective services and referral pathways through schools:
World Relief has set out to achieve the following objectives from the humanitarian interventions in the affected communities through emergency school meals for the improved learning opportunities, including access to safe, protective, inclusive and quality education, recreation, life-skills messages and psycho-social support activities to children in Koch, Guit (Unity State) and Fangak County (Jonglei State).
The planned intervention aims at providing not only the emergency school meals and transfer of food resources to entire families that is conditional upon school enrollment and regular attendance of children and building the capacities of education actors (teachers) and communities (PTA) in protecting the rights of children for education in this humanitarian crisis. Thus the project will also provide safe, inclusive and protective learning spaces, environmentally friendly and local building materials will be used where possible, to minimize environmental impact) with gender segregated WASH facilities and teaching and recreational materials. Additionally, supporting recruited EiE volunteer teachers through incentives, according to recent national and cluster guidelines and standards. The project will give special attention to girls’ education as their enrollment rate is very low and the dropout rate is very high in the country. This vulnerable segment of the society will be primary targets of the project as they are victims of harmful traditional and cultural practices.

title.narrative: Provision of life-saving protection assistance and services to vulnerable, conflict-affected children in Ayod, Jonglei State

description.narrative:
With the proposed project INTERSOS intends to guarantee continuation of its ongoing CP response in Ayod County that came to an end 31st July due to end of funds. The proposed intervention aims at strengthening individual case management and elaboration of case plans for unaccompanied, orphans and children with protection concerns, including children formerly recruited in armed forces of armed groups (CAAFAG) through CP helpdesks including provision of referrals to other services (education, health, NFIs, nutrition). Individual psychosocial support (PSS) activities will be provided (2/3 locations) to decrease children’s psychosocial distress, which is a result of protracted exposure to violence. Additionally, INTERSOS intends to keep its services within 2 CFS in Ayod County (Jiech, Mogok). CFS will be used as the entry point for the wider systems’ building component of the project. This critical intervention enables children who are exposed to an elevated level of violence and stress to participate in activities that help them gain a sense of normality, thus mitigating the possible negative developmental impacts. The CFS will be staffed with qualified CP staff as well as community volunteers with the appropriate set of skills and interest in working with children, who will undergo an intensive training in child protection and CFS management, followed by ongoing mentoring and coaching by INTERSOS Child Protection staff. Case management and community intervention will be implemented in all three locations. In addition, the project aims to strengthen the community-based networks to prevent and respond to violence against children by directly involving parents, caregivers and through enhancing the role of the recently formed CBCPNs, through regular workshops aimed at reinforcing community mechanism to responds to CP violations, and to enhance their resilience, strengthen positive coping mechanisms, supportive parenting skills and positive discipline. This is coupled with the continuous efforts INTERSOS undertakes to establish and strengthen community-based child protection systems and referral mechanisms through capacity building among community members, delivering knowledge on violation of child rights, signs and symptoms of different forms of abuse thereby contributing to the active identification of the most vulnerable children who suffer any form of harm, abuse, neglect or exploitation. As part of the continuous strengthening of community child protection systems the project will further implement awareness raising activities, including through public drama sessions, around child protection in emergencies. This will include a component of SGBV to ensure that children have access to the relevant information and services. This initiative will involve peer-to-peer education initiatives through the CFS. Additionally, adolescents will be supported to develop and lead on initiatives to increase local understanding of child protection risk factors and what kinds of steps children themselves can take to be protected from abuse, violence and exploitation through specific workshops and safety audit exercises. Finally, INTERSOS will provide activities for family tracing and reunification services in areas in continuation with what was done in recent months, including the provision of safe interim care arrangements for UASC, orphans and children leaving armed forces. Families that have adopted one or more UAC will be trained on the main principles of interim care provision and positive parenting skills.
Overall, INTERSOS wants to achieve a protective and child-friendly environment, free of any threats and harm for children, in Jiech, Karmoun and Mogok (Ayod County).

title.narrative: Provision of life-saving integrated primary health services; prevent detect and respond to disease outbreaks among the vulnerable populations in Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA).

description.narrative:
The project aims to contribute to the reduction of excess morbidity and mortality resulting from common infectious diseases, vector-borne diseases and epidemic-prone diseases as a consequence of severe food insecurity being driven by multiple shocks (effects of Covid-19, economic crisis and high food prices, impact of flooding on livelihood, and sub-national violence) among 28,000 (10,839 Men, 11281 Women, 2999 Girls and 2881 Boys) in Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA) of South Sudan particular Western part payams (Pibor and Verteth payams) . This aim will be obtained through the provision of time-critical, life-saving frontline quality health services, capacity building of health care workers, and strengthening of disease surveillance systems in the GPAA. The WHO Mobile Medical Teams (eMMT) provides integrated health services in deep field locations through mobile medical outreach modality. The eMMT comprise of experts from different fields of medicine often deployed strategically to provide gap-filling services in areas with serious unmet health needs. Such areas may include locations without static health facilities or those with no active health partners, locations with access constraints and those receiving high numbers of returnees, IDPs or refugees. The mobile clinics will offer outpatient consultations for common conditions, minor procedures, screening and treatment for malnutrition, immunization services, and referral services. Besides, WHO will train community health care workers to ensure continuity of health service provision in GPAA. Rapid assessments has been conducted in the GPAA to identify unmet needs and allow for ongoing health service provision, meanwhile, the Rapid Response Teams (RRT) will be deployed alongside the eMMTs to conduct case verification and investigation of suspected disease outbreaks. In addition, WHO will enhance capacity for disease surveillance and reporting to enhance detection of epidemic-prone diseases and continue to provide timely technical support for appropriate response by the Ministry of Health and other health partners The routine surveillance system will be enhanced through the deployment of mobile phone-based EWARS reporting by the static and mobile clinics attending to the needs of the community. This will enhance weekly reporting by facilities to ensure early detection of and response to disease outbreaks.
WHO will also conduct a risk assessment for common diseases such as measles and cholera in GPAA to ascertain the need for preventive vaccination campaigns and guide the planning process for preventive vaccination campaigns as well as secure adequate vaccines as guided by the risk assessment findings. Through its network of experts, both within and outside the country WHO will conduct targeted and focused capacity building of health workers working in the health facilities. The proposed capacity building will cover how to run mobile outreach programs, disease surveillance and outbreak response, case management, and infection prevention and control (IPC) within health facilities, and Clinical Management of Rape.
This project will also aim to procure and distribute emergency health kits to support health partners responding in the six prioritised Counties: Pibor, Akobo, Tonj East, Tonj North, Tonj South, and Aweil South. The distributed emergency health kits will benefit 377, 236 (Women151987, men 146029, girls 40402, and boys 38818).
This project is a scale up of the ongoing WHO emergency health in GPAA.

description.narrative: Humanitarian support through a multi-year agreement with IRC for the period 2018-2020.

Sida genomför årligen en humanitär allokeringsprocess i vilken samtliga humanitära kriser analyseras utifrån de humanitära behoven och där de mest relevanta väljs ut för finansiering genom Sidas humanitära strategiska partnerorganisationer. Det nu aktuella stödet till International Rescue Committee, United Kingdom, (IRC-UK), baseras på Sidas humanitära allokeringsprocess för år 2018, som färdigställdes under slutet av 2017. IRC-UK var en av tolv organisationer som utsågs 2013 till strategiska partnerorganisation för humanitärt stöd genom Sida. Valet baserades bl.a. på resultaten från en organisatorisk utvärdering genomförd av SIPU 2013.
IRC är en av världens ledande humanitära organisationer för att rädda liv och ge skydd till människor vars liv slagits sönder av konflikter och katastrofer. IRCs mervärde för Sida är att de når ut med humanitärt stöd till svårtillgängliga områden och kontexter. Man arbetar t.ex. i Syrien, Mali, Centralafrikanska Republiken (CAR), Demokratiska Republiken Kongo (DRK), Jemen och Nigeria, och försöker aktivt hitta fler och nya sätt att få ännu bättre tillträde i konfliktområden. IRC bedöms av Sida vara en speciellt kompetent part inom skyddsfrågor, med stor expertis inom könsbaserat våld (GBV), samt har en hög profil inom kontantbaserat stöd, cash. Sida har också överlag positiv erfarenhet av IRCs humanitära arbete som enligt Sidas erfarenhet håller hög tematisk kvalité och är relevant för Sidas humanitära strategi. I enlighet med en nyligen genomförd extern utvärdering (FCG 2017) av IRC-UK bekräftas denna bedömning. Utvärderingen bekräftar också att IRC har uppnått goda resultat i tidigare samarbete med Sidas humanitära enhet. IRC är också en "lärande" organisation som löpande testar nya arbetssätt och metoder baserat på behov och tidigare erfarenheter för att nå de mest sårbara. Man arbetar aktivt med att involvera och stärka mottagare, civila samhället och statliga aktörer i insatserna för att bidra till lokalt ägarskap. IRC genomför till största delen projekten i egen regi, dessutom vidareförmedlas 10% av projektmedlen till lokala organisationer. IRC är en aktiv part i lokala koordineringssystem och har ofta en framträdande roll inom skyddsklustret. Därutöver bekräftar utvärderingen (2017) att IRC har finansiellt och operationellt fungerande system på plats.
Det planerade humanitära stödet gäller perioden 2018-2020 med en allokering på 130,8 MSEK till IRC-UK för genomförande av insatser i 14 humanitära kontexter, RRM-medel (Rapid Response Mechanism) samt bidrag till metodutveckling och kapacitetsstöd. På IRCs begäran kommer en programansats på sektorbasis att påbörjas under perioden i tre av kontexterna: Nigeria, CAR och Kamerun. Anledningen är att IRC vill få möjlighet till ökad flexibilitet i genomförandet av projekten genom att Sida bidrar till de övergripande målen för hela IRCs sektorprogram i ett land. Dessutom föreslår IRC flerårigt stöd till CAR och Kamerun för att på ett bättre sätt kunna planera resurser och ha större framförhållning i stödet. Föreslaget program består därmed av följande delar och projekt:
1-ÅRIGT STÖD Nigeria, sektorprogramstöd, 6 MSEK Sektorstödet rör skydd och hälsa. Målet är att stödja internflyktingar och värdsamhällen som upplever sårbarhet och skyddsrisker och har begränsad möjlighet till att få basbehoven uppfyllda. Dessa ska få stöd att minska utsattheten för vattenburna sjukdomar samt att barn under 5 år och gravida och ammande kvinnor får förbättrad nutrition. IRC kommer att arbeta nära lokala organisationer för att förbättra deras kapacitet att fortsätta stödja utsatta människor. Geografiskt ska stöd ges till Maiduguri, Jere och Konduga.
Tchad, projektstöd, 5 MSEK Projektet rör förbättrat humanitärt stöd till hälsa, nutrition och skydd (framförallt för GBV) till utsatta människor i Tchad-sjö-området.
Mali, projektstöd, 5 MSEK Projektet rör stöd för återintegrering av barn och ungdomar som påvårkas av den väpnade konflikten i Mènaka-regionen.
Niger, projektstöd, 5 MSEK Projektet rör stöd till livräddande insatser genom förbättrad tillgång till basbehoven såsom vatten, mat, husrum, etc. i Diffa- och Agadez-regionerna.
Etiopien, projektstöd, 6 MSEK Projektet rör katastrofstöd i form av skydd och förbättrat ekonomiskt välbefinnande för människor som drabbats av torka i Somali- och Oromia-regionerna.
Sydsudan, projektstöd, 8 MSEK Projektet rör livräddande insatser och skydd för kvinnor och flickor i konfliktdrabbade områden i Juba och Rubkona.
Demokratiska Republiken Kongo, DRK, projektstöd, 6,5 MSEK Projektet rör livräddande och skyddsinsatser inom hälsa och GBV för konfliktdrabbad befolkning i Tanganyika-provinsen.
Jemen, projektstöd, 10 MSEK Projektet rör integrerat hälso- och GBV-stöd till konfliktdrabbade människor i Al'Dhale och Aden-provinserna.
Irak, projektstöd, 5.5 MSEK Projektet rör integrerat hälso- och GBV-stöd till konfliktdrabbade människor i Anbar, Duhok, Ninewa och Sulaymaniyah.
Libanon, projektstöd, 5 MSEK Projektet rör förbättrat skydd till syriska flyktingar (kvinnor och flickor) i större och mindre urbana samhällen i Libanon.
Syrien, projektstöd, 10 MSEK Projektet rör förbättrad hälsovård och skydd för konfliktdrabbad befolkning i nordvästra Syrien.
Libyen, projektstöd, 5 MSEK Projektet rör stöd till grundläggande hälso- och sjukvård (inklusive reproduktiv och psykisk sjukvård) till migranter och flyktingar i Tripoli.
2-ÅRIGT STÖD: CAR, sektorprogramstöd, 8 MSEK (år 2018); 8 MSEK (år 2019) Sektorstödet rör skydd, hälsa och ekonomiskt välbefinnande. Målet är att öka utsatta människors motståndskraft och skydd i svårtillgängliga områden genom att stärka lokalsamhällens skyddskapacitet och människors möjligheter till ekonomisk verksamhet. Geografiskt fokus är Ouham-Pende och Nana-Gribizi.
Kamerun, sektorprogramstöd, 6 MSEK (år 2018); 3 MSEK (år 2019) Sektorstödet rör skydd och ekonomiskt välbefinnande. Målet är att konfliktdrabbad befolkning ska kunna få sina basala behov tillgodosedda samt att bidra med stöd till speciellt drabbade och utsatta individer, samtidigt som man främjar en tidig återhämtning/resiliens. Geografiskt fokus är Mayo Sava och senare Logone et Chari.
RRM-INSATSER Av det initiala stödet för år 2018 utgör 20 MSEK stöd för korta snabba insatser genom RRM-mekanismen, vilket ger IRC flexibilitet att snabbt finansiera uppkomna eller förvärrade kriser i länder/regioner. Sida måste dock, enligt avtal, godkänna IRCs förslag på hur dessa RRM-medel ska allokeras.
METOD- OCH KAPACITETSSTÖD Detta stöd uppgår till totalt 5,1 MSEK för 2018 och rör klientanpassad metodutveckling (1,6 MSEK år 2018), samt metodutveckling för kontantbaserat stöd (1,5 MSEK år 2018), samt kapacitetsstöd för kvalitetsuppföljning, och lärande. Stödet beräknas minska under en tre-årsperiod, 2 MSEK (år 2018), 2 MSEK (år 2019) och 1,7 MSEK (år 2020).
En övergripande/indirekt administrationsavgift på 7% finns inlagd i varje enskild projektbudget ovan. Kostnaderna rör indirekta kostnader för service-funktioner för projektens genomförande genom IRCs operationella huvudkontor i New York samt IRCs underkontor i London, Storbritannien.
Den totala budgeten för 2018 är således 116,1 MSEK och för 2019 är budgeten initialt 13 MSEK och för 2020 initialt 1,7 MSEK, totalt 130,8 MSEK.
Upphandlingar genomförs till olika grad inom projekten. Variationen är stor med Jemens budget som innefattar den högsta andelen upphandling, ca 21 % av landets projektbudget, som kommer att framförallt bestå av förnödenheter i form av mediciner och medicinsk utrustning för distribution till hälsokliniker/sjukhus. IRC kommer också att vidareförmedla ca 10% av den totala Programbudgeten år 2018, till tre lokala organisationer i två kontexter (Jemen och Irak).
ORGANISATIONENS BAKGRUND
IRC etablerades år 1933 i USA och är en av världens ledande humanitära organisationer för att rädda liv och ge skydd till människor påverkade av konflikter och katastrofer. Deras verksamhet har sedan dess ökat och utvecklats och sträcker sig nu över 33 länder och IRC har mer än 10 000 medarbetare (varav 95 på sitt europeiska huvudkontor i London). IRCs globala organisation består av ett huvudkontor i New York som sköter den operationella verksamheten och har ansvaret för samtliga landkontor. IRC har också ett antal sub-huvudkontor på strategiska platser i världen, som t.ex. IRC-kontoret baserat i London, och flera regionala kontor. Tillsammans bildar dessa IRC-nätverket. IRC-UK är avtalspart till Sida.
ÖVRIGT
Sidas humanitära enhet och IRC har samarbetat sedan 2008 och IRC beviljades 2013 strategisk humanitär partnerskapsstatus hos Sida HUM. Sida bedömer att samtliga medel för programmet ska betalas ut omgående för att möjliggöra planering och uppstart av programmet till 1 maj 2018. Detta för att på bästa sätt möjliggöra planering och genomförande av den humanitära insatsen utan fördröjning.
Sidas stöd i aktuell insats är till största delen projektbaserad och IRC ges i avtalet flexibilitet att omallokera medel inom en total projektbudget (inklusive RRM-insatser, metod- och kapacitetsstöd) på upp till 10%. Detta bedöms vara nödvändigt för att på ett relevant, snabbt och ändamålsenligt sätt kunna möta humanitära behov. För ändringar över 10%, eller omallokeringar mellan projektbudgetar, krävs Sidas godkännande. För den del av programmet som är programbaserad, kommer IRC att ges rätt att inom ett sektorprogram fritt fördela medel inom de projekt i landet som bedöms lämpligast. Härigenom ges IRC en hög grad av flexibilitet avseende sektorprogrammens utformning.
Bedömningspromemorian har skrivits på engelska med anledning av att engelskspråkig personal i fält är delaktig i beredning och uppföljning av insatsen, i enlighet med Generaldirektörens beslut om Sidas språkvalsmatris med tillämpningsanvisningar från den 1 mars 2013.

The overall goal of the intervention was to respond to the world's worst humanitarian crises and help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. IRC titled the intervention "Survive, Recover and Thrive: Improving Lives for Crisis Affected People".
The intervention has included the implementation of 64 projects over the three-year period from 1 May 2018 31 March 2021. The intervention has included 38 humanitarian country projects, 20 Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) projects and six Methods Development and Capacity Building projects, providing lifesaving assistance to conflict affected and vulnerable people in 22 countries. Total expenditure has been 442 MSEK.

description.narrative:
The intervention has provided assistance to more than 2.8 million people across 22 countries in IRCs key outcome areas - health, safety, economic well-being, education and power. More than 1.1 million beneficiaries were in the health sector, some 469,000 received protection assistance, and almost a quarter of a million received WASH support. Over the course of the three years, 62% of beneficiaries were women and girls.
A few examples of results at country level:
In Nigeria, annual allocations over the three years have contributed to longer term behavioural change within the targeted communities. Specifically, programming has supported better health seeking behaviours and understanding of water borne diseases through continued messaging within the same communities. This has resulted in a significant reduction in cases of acute watery diarrhoea.
In Yemen support under Year 1 and 2 focused on Integrated health and gender-based violence support for conflict affected populations of Al Dhale and Aden governorates. In Year 3, IRC adapted the response to the COVID-19 pandemic and evolving restrictions on access. As well as delivering extensive support to health outcomes through mobile health team and support health facilities, lifesaving GBV services were delivered in remote areas, through women and girls' community centers and safe spaces.
In Democratic Republic of Congo, the rapid response mechanism (RRM) supported the Emergency Response to 2020 Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak in Equateur Province. IRC implemented a 4- month emergency project that provided health assistance by improving Infection Prevention and Control at eight health facilities in Mbandaka health zone and it included community engagement.
In Syria, IRC delivered Improving the Health and Safety of conflict-affected Populations in Northwest Syria in Year 1 and in Year 2 of the intervention. Conflict-affected Syrians thereby gained access to quality, integrated primary health care services, including effective GBV response.

title.narrative: Activity web page for IATI activity NL-1-PPR-23826
Coherent Danish support to South Sudan 2012-2015

description.narrative:
The Program Support Part ll will be phased in harmonized with part l, which in 2011 started Denmark's long-term development cooperation with Africa's newest country, South Sudan. The gradual implementation of the long-term cooperation takes the massive challenges that South Sudan faces after independence into account, where the country's own capacity is severely limited, and long term aid needs to operate in parallel with other instruments (political, humanitarian, peace/stability, military) The Program Support Part ll continues the previous focus on the connection between development and security/peace- and state build-up in accordance with South Sudan's own development plan and the principles in New Deal, where South Sudan is a pilot country. The goal is a peaceful and stable South Sudan capable of upholding the respect for Human Rights, Good Governance and access to social services. Part ll consolidates and enhances the two present components, Governance and Human Security, which are highly prioritized from political side in South Sudan. The support is directed through multilateral channels and is adjusted to national systems. In the area of governance the central and decentralised capacity of authorities will be strengthened with focus on accountability and transparency and service delivery to rights holders, meaningful participation in decision-making processes and access to social services at local level. In the area of security focus is on conflict prevention in marginalized local communities as well as the government's capability to take responsibility for the population's right to a life in security and anti-discrimination. The peace- and stabilization funds will focus on security sector reform.
Indicators for the program are developed on component level.

description.narrative: Support to education, training & deplyment of midwives through UNFPA co-financed by Canada.

United Nations Population Fund, UNFPA, har ansökt om ca 85 000 000 SEK i stöd för att genomföra projektet "Strengthening Midwifery Services in South Sudan" under 2015-18. Projektet utgör en del i UNFPAs bredare landprogram för att stärka barnmorskans roll i Sydsudan.
Insatsen avser uppnå 1) ökad tillgång till kvalitativ barnmorskeutbildning för hälsopersonal i Sydsudan; 2) ökad tillgång till hälsotjänster kopplat till kvinnor- och barns hälsa genom barnmorskor, sjuksköterskor, läkare och annan relevant vårdpersonal med ett miljömässigt hållbart och jämställt genomförande; 3) förbättrade förutsättningar för barnmorskor och obstetriker att verka i Sydsudan. Exempel på aktiviteter är finansiellt stöd för rekrytering av studenter till barnmorkseutbildningarna, anställning av kliniska handledare och mentorer, underhåll och inköp av undervisningsmaterial och teknisk utrustning, stöd till studenter för vidareutbildning på högre akademisk och teknisk nivå, tekniskt stöd till sydsudans hälsominiterium för att utveckla regelverk för legitimering, särskilda råd för yrkesgrupperna, strategier för personalförsörjning medmera. Sida bidrar även till en uppföljnings- och rapporteringstjänst inom projektet.
UNFPA är Sidas kontraktspartner och ansvarar för genomförandet av projektet. UNFPA vidareförmedlar medel till genomförandepartners, t ex de organisationer som ansvarar och driver utbildningsprogrammen på skolorna (Health Science Institutes). UNFPA samarbetar även med andra parnters som genom sin verksamhet är kopplade till projektet, framförallt Sydsudans hälsoministerium men även andra FN-organisationer och CSO. En utvärdering av projektets första fas från 2012-14 finansierad i huvudsak av kanadensiska Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development (DFATD), som utkom 2015 visar på god måluppfyllelse. Samtidigt har allvarlig kritik framförts mot projektets brister avseende jämställdhetsintegrering. Rekommendationer för att förbättra resultatuppfyllelse och kostnadseffektivitet har omhändertagits av UNFPA i utformningen av projektets andra fas, vilket borgar för ytterligare framsteg. UNFPA hävdar även att man avser omhänderta de rekomendationer som gjorts angående jämställdhetsintegrering.
Projektets totala budget är ca 368 MSEK för perioden 2015-20 och Sveriges bidrag uppgår till ca 85 MSEK för 2015-18. Ursprungligen hade hälsoministeriet gjort utfästelser om finansiellt stöd till projektet för 2015, men dessa kommer inte att infrias på grund av det ekonomiska läget. Sidas bidrag täcker upp för det uteblivna stödet från den sydsudanesiska regeringen under 2015, samt bidrar till en utökning av redan befintliga projektkomponenter. Det innebär bland annat att personer som nu befinner sig som internflyktingar kan avsluta avbrutna studier och att de pågående aktiviteter som finns kan löpa kontinuerligt som planerat under 2015. Sidas och Kanadas medel hanteras separat.

1 - Improved delivery of quality and gender-sensitive, and environmentally sustainable education for health care providers in South Sudan.2 - Improved delivery of environmentally sound and gender-sensitive Maternal Neonatal and Child Health (MNCH) services by midwives, nurses, clinical officers and other health care professionals such as doctors in targeted health facilities in South Sudan.3 - Strengthened enabling environment at the national and state level to facilitate for gender-sensitive midwifery and obstetrics practises in South Sudan.

description.narrative: Insatsen har i huvudsak fullföljts enligt plan trots att somliga områden och aktiviteter försenats. Sida har sedan tidigare beviljat en avtalsförlängning utan medelstillägg, då flera aktiviteter fördröjts till följd av bl.a. dåligt säkerhetsläge. Den planerade halvtidsutvärderingen har inte kunnat genomföras, utvärdering skulle ledas av Kanada/GAC men till följd av interna personalutmaningar hos GAC har utvärderingen senarelagts. UNFPA saknar följaktligen data för ett antal uppsatta RBM-indikatorer, men trots detta har flera resultat kunnat demonstrerats. Exempel på resultat: - Pågående utbildning av 366 barnmorske- och sjuksköterskestudenter vid 4 lärosäten. Andel avhopp har hållits inom målramen på max 10%. - Högre akademisk utbildning (BSc/MSc) för sydsudanesiska sjuksköterskor och barnmorskor vid lärosäten i grannländer (Tanzania och Kenya) som bidrar till högre kompetens hos framtida handledare och yrkesutövare. - Revidering av curriculum, med ökat fokus på jämställdhetsintegrering och GBV. Det nya carriculumet används nu av landets samtliga HSI (Health Science institutes/hälsovårdvetenskapliga institutioner). - Tillhandahållande av tjänster kopplade till SRHR och mödrabarnhälsovård vilket bidragit till förbättrad hälsa och överlevnad bland kvinnor och nyfödda. Exempelvis genom akutvård i samband med förlossnings- och graviditetskomplikationer, neonatalvård samt tillhandahållande av preventivmedel. - Etablerandet av 3 stycken ”one stop centres” som hjälper GBV-överlevare genom ett integrerat paket av medicinskt, psykosocialt, psykologiskt och juridiskt stöd. Centrerna har hittills behandlat 580 fall, av dessa har 73 tagits vidare till domstol där 46 fall slutat i fällande domar och resterande 27 fortfarande väntar på domslut. - Påverkansarbete genom exempelvis genom radioinslag och ”community sensitizations”-möten som nått 6,966 personer och syftat till att sprida information om GBV och bemöta sociala normer. Parallellt har vårdpersonal och olika andra strategiska partners utbildats i omhändertagande av GBV-överlevare. - Stöd till medlemsorganisationen för sjuksköterskor och barnmorskor i Sydsudan (SSNMA) vilket bidragit till fler medlemmar och en starkare organisation som driver professionens utveckling och verkan inom mödrabarnhälsa och SRHR. - Stöd som bidragit till att hälsodepartementet skapat ett interimsråd som påbörjat arbetet med att ta fram nya regelverk och registreringssystem för barnmorske- och sjuksköterskeyrket.

title.narrative: Emergency healthcare delivered through the PHCC, PHCU, Mobile Teams and iCCM packages targeting vulnerable and unreached host communities where IDPs are integrated in Fangak and Nyirol counties of former Jonglei State.

description.narrative:
The emergency that this project will address is the high rate of mortality from malaria, AWD, pneumonia, SAM with medical complications and outbreaks of measles, cholera and kala-azar. In the volatile context of GUN, the project will target IDPs recently displaced and newly displaced by conflict, and IDPs and host communities in PHCU locations without health services. Nyirol is rated as IPC 4 Emergency for February to May, but expected to deteriorate (IPC SS Oct 2017, FEWS Net, pg7). Catastrophic (IPC Phase 5) remains likely in parts of Nyirol, where households did not harvest and ongoing insecurity is limiting access to assistance and movement towards natural food sources (FEWS Net January 2018).
Two clinical packages will be delivered: PHCU and mobile teams for emergency outreach. A third package, the PHCC package for the treatment of SAM with medical complications and CMR will be delivered at one PHCC (Pultruk) with established stabilization center. To address access, coverage and service interruptions, the project will support: (1) case-finding medical outreaches from PHCUs to reach vulnerable HHs and conduct surveillance (2) emergency mobile teams to reach locations without PHCU services and to serve new and recently displaced people (3) one selected PHCC for the stabilization of SAM and CMR as well as referrals of patients needing specialized services for HIV/AIDS, TB and MPPSS. The project will provide skilled health workers for the PHCUs, mobile teams and PHCC-based stabilization centers, and provide support to conduct the outreaches to bomas not served by static facilities, and for mobile team outreaches in an emergency. The project will provide equipment, supplies to maintain services from PHCU facilities and add transportation for implementation of emergency mobile team outreaches.
Estimates for Nyirol show 49,335 IDPs as of October 2017. Recent conflict in Waat where the population has been displaced to Keew has raised the displaced population by at least 16,000 according to local authorities and CMA’s on-ground teams.
Data from the fourth quarter of 2017 indicates the leading causes of morbidity were: malaria, diarrhea and pneumonia (CMA HMIS Data October-December 2017). During 2017, 3 cases of cholera were confirmed and 6 other cases were suspected. Nutrition Cluster data shows a GAM rate of 25.7 for children U5 and 35.2 for PLW. The increase in SGBV has heightened the need for CMR for the survivors of rape.
The project will fill the critical humanitarian gap of lack of access to frontline lifesaving healthcare services for the most vulnerable children U5, and PLW of newly displaced and unserved IDP populations. To address this gap, PHCU and mobile team clinical packages will be scaled-up along with stabilization center services to treat SAM with medical complication at Pultruk PHCC.
Project objective 1 aims to improve access to healthcare for conflict-affected populations with emphasis on malaria control, AWD and pneumonia. Project objective 2 aims to prevent, detect and respond to epidemic prone disease outbreaks especially kala-azar, measles and cholera through both static services and emergency mobile team outreaches, including surveillance to detect new outbreaks. Emphasis will be on preventing infection, water quality and waste management when delivering cholera treatment. Project objective 3 will improve access to essential clinical health services that are inclusive and implemented with dignity and targeted to the specific needs of women and adolescent girls including essential CMR services.
An estimated 14,286 outpatient consultations will be achieved, of which 4,143 will be children U5, and 1,142 PLW women. To ensure the project achieves gender equality in access to health services, communities will be organized to provide protection for vulnerable women, adolescent girls and children so they are not impeded when access to services is needed.

title.narrative: To reduce morbidity and mortality of vulnerable population through the provision of quality primary health care services

description.narrative:
To reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve resilience and psychosocial wellbeing of vulnerable populations in Leer through providing access to quality Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM), management of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) and Mental Health and PsychoSocial Support (MHPSS) services, integrated alongside Medair’s emergency nutrition and WASH programming.
Medair will implement a flexible model of iCCM, to treat the main diseases in children under 5, and will provide other mobile, community-based services, including management of SGBV and mental health and psychosocial support. Recurrent insecurity, frequent population displacements and emergency levels of malnutrition lead to high levels of health needs in this vulnerable population. Insecurity has often disrupted facility-based health services in this area. Medair’s lifesaving community-based mobile services will address prioritised emergency needs in the most vulnerable population groups in an integrated manner which is flexible to adapt to further displacement and conflict, and strengthens the future resilience of this population.
A network of mother-to-mother ‘Cascade Groups’ is supported by staff trained in appropriate modalities of mental health and psychosocial support. Child-friendly spaces complement Medair’s integrated programming in Leer. Additionally, management of SGBV (including Clinical Management of Rape) is undertaken by trained staff within the community, also linking survivors with mental health and psychosocial support services and other protection services as appropriate. Medair seeks to facilitate provision of treatment according to the mhGAP-HIG, in line with the BPHNS, through appropriately-qualified health workers employed by Medair. Medair will train and supervise these staff to provide first line, non-specialised management of acute and chronic mental health conditions such as acute stress, grief, depression and psychosis. During the period of the project, Medair will ensure regular follow-up of beneficiaries identified with mental health conditions.

description.narrative: This project is focusing on provision of preventive and curative integrated primary health care services, including both emergency and routine immunization to eliminate vaccine preventable diseases, and screening and treatment of childhood illnesses through health facilities, outreach and mobile services to reach the IDPs, through provision of core pipeline supplies and technical assistance.

title.narrative: Campaigns for Women's Rights in SS

description.narrative: This project will use entertainment programmes to educate the population in Western Equatoria Region of South Sudan on all forms ofGender based violence to women. Consultative community meetings will be held with various stakeholders to identify the common formsGBVs which we will reproduce in form of dramas, puppetry shows, dance, vocal performances and visual artist to clearly promote Women rights. The plays will be performed and popularized in a manner to ridicule people who violate women rights.

participating-org.narrative: Mundri Active Youth Association (MAYA) is a nonprofit making, non political civil society organization, founded in 2004 by the youths of Greater Mundri Counties (Mundri West/East and Mvolo) to strengthen and empower the community capacity in the field ofCivic Education, Health, Creative Arts and Socio-economic activities. MAYA is registered with the Ministry of Humanitarian affairs and Disaster Management (RRC) Juba under serial number 137. Since its establishment, the Association has been actively involved in community empowerment in Greater Mundri with a specific focus on negative cultural practices that promote violation of women and children rights, dangers of forced and early marriages, peace building and human rights principles through theatre techniques (such as drama/puppetry shows), film production, Trainings/workshops, focus group discussions and community meetings thus enhancing their understanding on the issues affecting the community.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has applied for a renewed strategic partnership with Sida during 2021-2025.
NRC has applied as well to Sida for funding of 364.5 million SEK to carry out “the Humanitarian Programme for 2021” in 26 humanitarian crisis settings: Afghanistan, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Honduras, El Salvador, Mexico, Palestine, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania/Burundi, Uganda, Venezuela, Yemen. The application includes provision of 40 million SEK to replenish the Rapid Response Mechanism funding instrument and 7 individual projects for method, capacity-building and coordination.
The intervention’s tentative total budget is 4 263 200 000 Norwegian krona (NOK), that the organisation is financing with Sida’s funding in a proportion of 8% approximately. Other donors, like the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, DG ECHO, UNHCR, etc. are the largest contributors, besides a dozen of other donors in agreement with NRC. Sida provides NRC with the opportunity to allocate resources flexibly within individual country programmes (Programme-Based Approach – PBA). ¬ NRC's catalytic support for coordination and capacity building contributes greatly to the link between humanitarian aid, development and peace. NRC's advocacy work and activities enable, at least contribute to, sustainable solutions for refugees and displaced people in a significant way in cooperation with other actors. In the long run, the NRC will reduce humanitarian needs. The NRC prioritizes self-sufficiency in its programs. The NRC's analysis capability, not least through its Internal Displacement Monitoring Center (IDMC), is an advantage for relevant programming according to the nexus orientations. Among the 26 crises in NRC's portfolio that Sida prioritizes, there are 15 where Sida implements Sweden's development strategies in synergy with humanitarian aid.
In 2022 support NRC with 455,5 MSEK in total of Sida’s humanitarian funding, according to the following breakdown: - The grant will support NRC humanitarian programmes in 23 crises settings that Sida has prioritized through its needs-based allocation model, with 288.5 MSEK during 2022: Afghanistan, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Colombia and region, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Mozambique, Niger, Nigeria, Palestine, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Venezuela, Yemen - As multi-annual funding for emergency response in DR Congo, Mali and Nigeria is initiated in 2022, the grant will provide as well NRC with outstanding financial commitments from Sida, estimated 104 MSEK for 2023-2024. - NRC emergency response in sudden onset crises will be supported through Sida’s Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) window with 50 MSEK for 2022. - NRC’s method and capacity development projects for Protection, Environment and the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) will receive 13 MSEK, including 3 MSEK from Sida/Globen for IDMC. Sida’s contribution to NRC for 2022 will cover around 6.5% of NRC’s total financial requirements of the supported programmes and projects. It will provides humanitarian services to almost 9 million persons (53% female). HUM adds 50 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in Ukraine benefiting 90,000 people with protection, shelter, WaSH and cash assistance. Decision 5 April. Amendment nr. 5. HUM adds 7.5 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in Cameroon from the 2022 mid-year allocation (food security, legal advice for 600 households/4200 individuals in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga). Decision 9 June 2022. Contract amendment No 6. HUM adds 10 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in South Sudan from the end-of-the-year allocation. Decision 16 November 2022 nr 2022-002341. Contract amendment No 7.
2023 NRC will receive a total of SEK 659.5 million (2023-2025) of Sida's humanitarian funding to implement: - humanitarian operations in 23 crisis areas in 2023: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Colombia, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Iraq, Yemen, Jordan, Cameroon, Kenya, Lebanon, Mali, Mozambique, Niger, Palestine, Sudan, South Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine and Venezuela. NRC has also applied for SEK 244 million to continue its humanitarian programmes in Yemen, Cameroon, South Sudan, Syria and Venezuela in 2024 and 2025. - The application also includes SEK 50 million for the Rapid Reaction Mechanism (RRM) - and SEK 40 million in support of four multi-year projects for methodological support and capacity building: Environment, Protection, Access, IDMC (18.5 MSEKin 2023, 21.5 MSEK in 2024-2025). Decision dated ... March 2023. Contract amendment No 8.
NRC targets 7.7 million unique beneficiaries in total within Sida-funded humanitarian programmes in 2023, (52% female), who will receive protection and humanitarian services from NRC: Education, WASH, Shelter and settlement, Food security and livelihoods, including multi-purpose cash assistance, Protection, Legal assistance, Humanitarian mediation (community-based peace-building). Advocacy and support to humanitarian coordination and durable solution to displacements working groups in the field are part of NRC's engagement that Sida is funding. NRC's annual budget 2023 in the settings and thematics prioritized by Sida amounts to 5620 million Norwegian crowns in total. Sida's share weighs so far 8% of it: NRC's third largest donor whose cumulated 2021-2025 grant is 80% softly earmarked (programme-based approach) and 34% multi-year.
Earlier granted multi-year funding for 2023 was disbursed in January (52 MSEK) in support to continued humanitarian operations in DR Congo, Mali and Nigeria with strong emphasis on emergency response.

Norwegian Refugee Council - Norska flyktingrådet (NRC) - har ansökt om ett förnyat partnerskap med Sida 2021-2025.
2021 NRC har dessutom ansökt om finansiering på 364,5 miljoner SEK för att genomföra humanitära insatser i 26 humanitära krisområden under 2021: Afghanistan, Kamerun, Centralafrikanska republiken, Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Demokratiska Republiken Kongo, Eritrea, Etiopien, Iran, Irak, Jordanien, Kenya, Libanon, Libyen, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Honduras, El Salvador, Mexiko, Palestina, Somalia, Sydsudan, Sudan, Tanzania / Burundi, Uganda, Venezuela och Jemen. Ansökan inkluderar även 40 miljoner kronor för den humanitära snabbmekanismen (RRM) och 20 miljoner kronor i stöd till sju projekt för metodstöd, kapacitetsuppbyggnad och samordning.
Den aktuella budgeten för NRC:s hela humanitära program 2021 uppgår till 4 263 200 000 NOK, varav Sidas del för närvarande utgör ca 8%. Sida ger NRC möjligheten att nyttja resurser flexibelt inom varje enskilt landprogram, (enligt så kallad Programme-Based Approach – PBA)
Humanitär-Utveckling-Fred Nexus NRC bidrar i hög grad till arbetet för att sammankoppla humanitärt bistånd med freds- och utvecklingsinsatser. Organisationens strävan att effektivisera biståndet genom katalytiskt stöd till samordning och kapacitetsbyggande insatser bidrar till denna ansats. I samarbetet med andra organisationer möjliggör och bidrar NRC:s verksamhet och påverkansarbete till att stärka hållbara lösningar för flyktingar och människor som har blivit tvångsfördrivna och bidrar därmed till att på sikt minska de humanitära behoven. Även krisdrabbade människors möjligheter till självförsörjning prioriteras. NRC:s analyskapacitet är en styrka som bidrar till att programmeringen anpassas till en nexus-ansats och den analys som genomförs av NRC:s internationella center för övervakning av tvångsförflyttning (IDMC) är av stor vikt för dessa analyser. 19 av de 26 kriser i NRC:s portfölj som Sida finansierar avser länder där Sverige även bedriver utvecklingssamarbete vilket öppnar för möjligheter till synergier med humanitärt bistånd.
2022 NRC ska få totalt 455,5 miljoner kronor av Sidas humanitära finansiering, enligt följande fördelning:
- Sida kommer att stödja NRC:s humanitära program i 23 krissituationer som Sida har prioriterat genom sin behovsbaserade allokeringsmodell för 2022, med 288,5 miljoner kronor :Afghanistan, Centralafrikanska republiken, Colombia och regionen (Ecuador, Panamà), Demokratiska republiken Kongo, Etiopien, Irak, Jemen, Jordanien, Kamerun, Kenya, Libanon, Libyen, Mali, Moçambique, Niger, Nigeria, Palestina, Somalia, Sudan, Sydsudan, Syrien, Uganda, Venezuela.
- Flerårig finansiering för NRC :s humanitära program i Demokratiska republiken Kongo, Mali och Nigeria inleds 2022 och Sida har för ändamålet att ta i anspråk 104 miljoner kronor från kommande års anslag från erhållen Bemyndiganderam förutsatt att Riksdagen anvisar tillräckliga medel.
- NRC:s akuta insatser vid plötsligt uppkomna kriser kommer att stödjas genom Sidas snabbinsatsmekanism (RRM) under 2022 med 50 miljoner kronor.
- NRC:s metod- och kapacitetsstärkande projekt för skydd, miljö och IDMC (Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre) kommer under 2022 att få 13 miljoner kronor, varav 3 miljoner kronor från Sida/Globen för IDMC.
Sidas bidrag till NRC för 2022 kommer att täcka cirka 6,5 % av NRC:s totala finansiella behov för de stödda programmen och projekten. Det kommer att tillhandahålla humanitära tjänster till nästan 9 miljoner människor (53 % kvinnor) i Afghanistan, Kamerun, Centralafrikanska republiken, Colombia och regionen, Demokratiska republiken Kongo, Etiopien, Irak, Jordanien, Kenya, Libanon, Libyen, Mali, Moçambique, Niger, Nigeria, Palestina, Somalia, Sydsudan, Sudan, Syrien, Uganda, Venezuela och Jemen.
HUM lägger till 50 MSEK för NRC:s landprogram 2022 i Ukraina som gynnar 90,000 människor med skydd, tak över huvudet, WaSH samt kontantbistånd. Beslut 5 April. Avtalförändring nr 5.
HUM lägger till 7,5 MSEK för NRC:s landprogram 2022 i Kamerun från halvsårsanslaget 2022 (livsmedelsförsörjning, juridik rådgivning för 600 husshållen/4200 individer i Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava och Mayo Tsanaga). Beslut 9 juni 2022. Avtalförändring nr 6.
HUM lägger till 10 MSEK för NRC:s landprogram 2022 i Sydsudan från slutsåranslaget. Beslut 16 november 2022, 2022-002341. Avtalförändring nr 7.
2023 NRC ska få totalt 659.5 miljoner kronor (2023-2025) av Sidas humanitära finansiering för att genomföra: - humanitära insatser i 23 krisområden under 2023: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Centralafrikanska republiken, Colombia, Demokratiska republiken Kongo, Etiopien, Irak, Jemen, Jordanien, Kamerun, Kenya, Libanon, Mali, Moçambique, Niger, Palestina, Sudan, Sydsudan, Syrien, Uganda, Ukraina och Venezuela. NRC har dessutom ansökt om 244 miljoner kronor för att kunna fortsätta sina humanitära program i Jemen, Kamerun, Sydsudan, Syria och Venezuela under 2024 och 2025. - ansökan inkluderar även 50 miljoner kronor till den humanitära snabbinsatsmekanismen (RRM) - och 40 miljoner kronor i stöd till fyra fleråriga projekt för metodstöd och kapacitetsuppbyggnad: Miljö, Skydd, Tillträde, IDMC (18,5 under 2023, 21,5 under 2024-2025).

Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is Norway's largest international humanitarian organisation and widely recognized as a leading field-based displacement agency within the international humanitarian community. NRC is the INGO receiving the largest contribution from Sida's Humanitarian Unit to INGOs so far, based on experience of successful partnerships, NRC's capacities to respond at scale and its coverage of crises that Sida is prioritizing through the needs-based allocation approach. NRC receives approximately 8% of Sida's humanitarian unit's annual budget appropriation.
The objectives of NRC can be summarized as follows: "To protect the rights of displaced and vulnerable people during crisis, to provide assistance meeting their immediate humanitarian needs, to prevent further displacement and to contribute to durable solutions, and to provide expertise as a strategic partner to humanitarian systems and actors." NRCs main activity is delivery of humanitarian assistance through programme activities in the field. NRC specializes in six areas of expertise, or "core competencies": shelter and settlements; livelihoods and food security; information, counselling and legal assistance (ICLA); education; camp management; and water, sanitation and hygiene promotion (WASH). Protection is lifted up as a new core competency of NRC since 2021. NRC engages closely with the affected populations to understand their needs and capacities, ensuring it tailors its assistance accordingly and involve them in the entire programme cycle, from design through implementation to evaluation. NRC advocates for respect for the rights of displaced and vulnerable people.
In 2021, the NRC Board approved the Global Strategy 20222025. The strategy sets out four sub-objectives for areas that NRC will continue to strengthen and further institutionalize, namely, 1. assistance to hard-to-reach populations, 2. humanitarian policy, 3. protection, and 4. durable solutions. It also points to four areas of work that will be accelerated through expanded engagement and investments: i) advocacy, ii) climate and environment, iii) collaboration with local actors, and iv) quality programming.
NRCs work is divided into three pillars: humanitarian assistance, advocacy and expert deployment. Sida's Humanitarian Unit funding will continue prioritizing mainly the first pillar through funding of the humanitarian country programmes in line with HRPs and the RRPs and through the RRM funding. To some extent, Sida will support as well the second pillar of advocacy which is integrated in the humanitarian country programmes and implemented by NRC's method, thematic and capacity development projects supported by Sida. Sida will provide NRC with only a punctual support to the third pillar, through funding to CashCap which is deploying experts to the field for invigorating cash assistance working groups (17 in 2020 to 16 countries).

Sidas contribution to NRC for 2022 will cover around 6.5% of NRCs total financial requirements of the supported programmes and projects. It will provides humanitarian services to almost 9 million persons (53% female). HUM adds 50 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in Ukraine benefiting 90,000 people with protection, shelter, WaSH and cash assistance. Decision 5 April. Amendment nr. 5. HUM adds 7.5 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in Cameroon from the 2022 mid-year allocation (food security, legal advice for 600 households/4200 individuals in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga). Decision 9 June 2022. Contract amendment No 6.
From Conclusion on performances September 2022:
NRC foresees that 8,986,125 persons (53.4% female) will benefit from NRC's humanitarian services in 2022 in 35 crisis settings. It is however likely that NRC will over-achieve again its initial target.
NRC is on a continued trajectory of growth in the delivery of cash and vouchers to people affected by displacement. The trend should be brought at scale, given the multiplying effect on empowered beneficiaries. Impacts of Multi-purpose cash assistance could be researched and highlighted further by NRC for promoting cash assistance as the best option, becoming hopefully the default method for the provision of humanitarian assistance everywhere and for all actors.
Education was a declining sector for NRC in 2020 and 2021 due to closure of schools under Covid-19. It generated many new protection risks, like early marriage for girls, early pregnancies, drop-out of school-aged children from education, and psychosocial needs. Restart of education services is going on in 2022. Meanwhile, following the pandemic, NRC saw the rapid scale up of psychosocial support programme, the Better Learning Programme (BLP). Building on lessons learned from the Middle East region, it has rolled-out BLP to both Central and West Africa (CWA) and Latin America. To reach children stuck at home, NRC developed a BLP smartphone application for both parents and teachers.
Protection
NRC developed Minimum Standards on Safe and Inclusive Programming (protection mainstreaming) which are now incorporated into the Global Strategy (2022-2025) as a critical component of programme quality. Mainstreamed and integrated protection are generating increasingly protection outcomes within NRC's humanitarian assistance.
Protection is evolving into a full new core competence of NRC as from 2022 with stand-alone protection capacities and interventions wherever relevant.
NRC has been essential in hosting the Sida-funded IASC protection policy review in 2021.
Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) in particular for Housing, Land and Property issues (HLP) remain the domain of excellence of NRC that only few other protection actors can match and replace. Solved documentation problems related to legal identity, civil status and property is key to the protection of the displaced people, including children and women.
Inclusive programming
NRC reports a systematic engagement with communities in term of participation to the design and orientation of the response.
Its ambition to shift resolutely towards increased equal to equal partnerships, especially to mobilize local resources among the civil society, was not yet articulated in 2021 in term of localized partnerships and will be hopefully worked through during the strategic cycle 2022-2025. NRC has a long way to go, as its is mainly implementing interventions by itself.
Sida's helpdesk on gender had reservation about NRC's effective gender mainstreaming in programming and reporting. The outcome is certainly better, in most cases, than reported. NRC has to ensure that it captures this dimension in its programme documents (both applications and reports).
Data security and protection risk management do not give visibility to the assistance and the protection services delivered by NRC to LGBTQI people. Sida should respect this and not request specific dis-aggregated data capturing this beneficiary groups. Sida has evidence that NRC protection work is non-discriminatory and reaches out effectively people with specific needs, including LGBTQI people.
Coordination
NRC is a key asset of the global and local humanitarian systems for its dedicated participation to coordination forums, bringing to them its principled approach and expertise for humanitarian action: the IASC, humanitarian country teams, advisory groups, clusters, hosted and facilitated NGO forums, working groups in many areas and sectors, including durable solutions to displacements. It is not infrequent that NRC co-leads protection, shelter, food security, education, camp management clusters. Such constructive participation is making a difference and is likely to improve the humanitarian system.
Advocacy 2021
NRC continued its advocacy work on Sanctions and Counter-terrorism measures affecting humanitarian service delivery, in particular in Afghanistan.
NRC released its flagship annual report on the Worlds Most Neglected Displacement Crises, which analyses displacement crises based on lack of funding, lack of media attention, and lack of international political and diplomatic initiatives.
NRC's Secretary General became the Eminent Person of the Grand Bargain. Through this role, NRC is in a unique position to steer reforms aimed at improving the system, through efforts such as ensuring that implementing organisations receive a critical mass of quality funding and working towards making the aid system more localized.
NRC's Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC), co-funded by HUM and INTEM at Sida, launched its 2021 Global Report on Internal Displacement (GRID), featuring a special focus on disaster displacement and the impacts of climate change, exploring the intersections of climate, disasters, and internal displacement.
Most country offices are producing frequent advocacy documents about the rights of displaced populations, voiceless affected communities and humanitarian contexts that are highly appreciated and of good quality.
Humanitarian policy-making 2021
As part of NRCs Global Strategy process, a Climate and Environment Strategy 2030 was developed, focusing on strengthening NRCs response in the areas of climate adaptation, access to clean energy, and reduced environmental footprint. NRC also signed the Climate and Environment Charter for Humanitarian Organisations, which entails a commitment to work on climate adaptation and mitigation, including through setting public time-bound targets for emissions reductions. NRC also initiated work to establish environmental minimum standards for its programmes. These were developed for shelter and settlements, WASH, livelihood and food security, and emergency response.
Nexus
NRC has drawn lessons from pilot experience of 'humanitarian mediation' in Mali, DRC and CAR during 2017-2020 that was funded by Sida/FRED (#11611). The external final evaluation concluded that this pilot phase of introducing peace-building within the scope of NRC's programmes would deserve to be followed by another pilot experience correcting the shortcomings of the initiative that was found not fully relevant, efficient and successful. The lack of capacities in implementing the new programme in three very challenging contexts was pointed out. It does not mean that NRC should abandon the idea to try again. Preventing protection risks, including those resulting to forced displacements, by mitigating tensions and antagonism between communities, is highly needed in crisis contexts. But it requires an expertise and partnerships that cannot be built overnight. NRC should be encouraged to persist.
NRC is better placed for linking emergency and recovery when it explores and supports durable solutions to displacement. The development leg of the nexus falls within NRC's natural mandate, although it cannot or should not be resourced by Sida's humanitarian funding, but rather by development budget-lines. NRC is meant to support IDPs and refugees before, during and after displacements and to accompany them until displacements cease to affect them, because they could be repatriated, resettled or locally integrated in a sustainable and dignified way. It is unclear whether durable solutions interventions of NRC are budgeted within NRC's country humanitarian programmes that are submitted to Sida or resourced within longer-term strategies. It is not unusual that Sida colleagues visiting NRC in the field give as a feedback that NRC's interventions are getting near development work, because the response is protracted and because it addresses rather recovery needs than life-saving needs. HUM is however very clear to NRC in its dialogue by highlighting that HUM funding is for humanitarian interventions only and within the frameworks of OCHA's and UNHCR's humanitarian appeals, if they exist. It is however often difficult, if one should ever do it, to draw a clear and separate line between humanitarian action and recovery/resilience/durable solutions. In some countries, especially in protracted refugee / displacement situations that are no more acute crises, support to care and maintenance, to self-reliance and to durable solutions, like in Jordan for instance, represents the bulk of NRC's programme, while emergency life-saving and protection services are less necessary. Such interventions would be better supported by longer-term development or recovery budget-lines, within the framework of the Global Compact for Refugees and the Comprehensive Refugee Response Framework. Development donors are increasingly getting involved, including Sida, but too slow, too late and too short. Meanwhile, assisting aid-dependent IDPs and refugees throughout the years / decades of their displacement career, like the Palestinan refugees and many other caseloads, remains resourced mainly by humanitarian budget-lines, including Sida's.
Sida's assessment on performance and results
Alike many other actors in the sector, NRC excels in reporting activities and outputs, but should be better in catching what changes and impacts its interventions have resulted to ultimately on assisted communities. The reporting of data and results does not provide necessarily an accurate and consolidated overview of what NRC has achieved. Sida has notified NRC that it should provide dis-aggregated data by age in targeting and reporting which is a norm.
NRC has still a long way to go for building programme partnerships and localizing its programmes. NRC channeled Sida funding in 2021 to only 15 partners in total, including 4 INGOs, for a very little proportion of the total humanitarian funding received from Sida, below 1%, less than in 2019 and 2020 (3%). NRC is however party to many consortia and excels in cooperating with local authorities and actors, and building their capacitries, although not through financial transactions.
Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM)
HUM granted 40 MSEK to NRC in 2021 as the annual RRM allocation amount, without replenishment during the course of the year, as in 2019. NRC managed to utilize this emergency response funding window sparingly until October 2021, supporting 14 projects in 13 countries. In 2022, the allocation amounted to 50 MSEK; this funding allocation is almost completely exhausted (4 MSEK left), after support to 12 projects in 12 countries has been approved.
